name: Beta-Quartz (High Quartz, SiO2)
description: The high-temperature polymorph of quartz, stable above 573 °C (at ambient pressure). Crystallizes in the hexagonal system.

name: Alpha-Cristobalite (Low Cristobalite, SiO2)
description: A low-temperature, tetragonal polymorph of cristobalite. Often occurs as a metastable phase in volcanic rocks and opal.

name: Beta-Cristobalite (High Cristobalite, SiO2)
description: The high-temperature cubic polymorph of cristobalite, stable above ~267 °C and sometimes found stabilized at room temperature in glasses.

name: Alpha-Tridymite (Low Tridymite, SiO2)
description: A complex, low-symmetry polymorph of tridymite found in terrestrial volcanic rocks and meteorites as a metastable phase.

name: Beta-Tridymite (High Tridymite, SiO2)
description: The high-temperature hexagonal polymorph of tridymite. Forms typically between 870 °C and 1470 °C.

name: Stishovite (SiO2 High-Pressure Polymorph)
description: An extremely dense, high-pressure polymorph of silica with octahedrally coordinated silicon (rutile structure). Forms during meteorite impacts.

name: Keatite (SiO2 Synthetic Polymorph)
description: A synthetic tetragonal polymorph of silica. Rarely found in nature, but can form hydrothermally in ultra-high-pressure environments or as intermediate phases.

name: Moganite (SiO2 Monoclinic Polymorph)
description: A monoclinic polymorph of silica occurring widely in microcrystalline silica such as chalcedony, chert, and flint.

name: Seifertite (SiO2 Ultra-High-Pressure)
description: An ultra-high-pressure polymorph of silica found in Martian and Lunar meteorites, with an alpha-PbO2-type structure.

name: NIST SRM 1976 (Corundum / α-Al2O3)
description: NIST Standard Reference Material 1976 (sintered alpha-alumina / corundum plate; Trigonal R-3c, a = 4.7589 Å, c = 12.9917 Å, Z = 6; PDF 00-046-1212) used for calibrating X-ray powder diffraction instrument sensitivity, line positions, and peak profiles.

name: NIST SRM 640 (Silicon Profile Standard)
description: NIST Standard Reference Material 640 (Silicon powder) is the primary line position standard. The lattice parameter is certified with extreme precision. Used worldwide to mitigate instrumental zero-shift and sample displacement errors.

name: NIST SRM 660 (Lanthanum Hexaboride, LaB6)
description: NIST SRM 660 (LaB6) is utilized for calibration of diffraction line profiles and line position. It possesses very narrow intrinsic line profiles, ideal for instrumental broadening (FWHM) correction and size/strain analysis.

name: NIST SRM 676 (Alumina Phase Quant Standard)
description: NIST SRM 676a alpha-alumina (corundum) quantitative reference powder (Trigonal R-3c, a = 4.7589 Å, c = 12.9917 Å, Z = 6; PDF 00-046-1212, RIR I/Ic = 1.00) designed specifically for quantitative phase analysis and Rietveld internal standardization.

name: NIST SRM 674b (TiO2/ZnO/Cr2O3/CeO2)
description: Quantitative x-ray powder diffraction standard set (SRM 674b: rutile, zincite, eskolaite, cerianite). Used to calibrate equipment intensities and serve as internal standards for crystalline phase quantization.

name: Silicon (Si)
description: A hard, brittle crystalline solid with a blue-grey metallic lustre.

name: Zirconia (ZrO2)
description: Zirconium dioxide is a white crystalline oxide of zirconium.

name: Hydroxyapatite (Highly Crystalline)
description: Stoichiometric hexagonal hydroxyapatite (h-HAp, Ca/P = 1.667) with statistically disordered OH⁻ columns along the 63 screw axis, serving as the primary crystallographic reference for sintered bioceramics and plasma-sprayed coatings. Hexagonal P63/m (No. 176), a = 9.418 Å, c = 6.884 Å, Z = 1, PDF 00-009-0432.

name: Nano-Hydroxyapatite (Biomimetic)
description: Biomimetic nano-crystalline hydroxyapatite synthesized via controlled precipitation at physiological temperatures. Characterized by substantial line broadening due to nanoscale crystallites (<50nm) and inherent lattice strains, closely mimicking the morphological and crystallographic state of young mammalian bone mineral.

name: Carbonated Hydroxyapatite (Type-B)
description: Biological-grade Type-B carbonated hydroxyapatite featuring significant carbonate (CO3) substitution at phosphate (PO4) lattice sites. This ionic doping induces substantial crystalline disorder, reduces symmetry, and dramatically increases bio-resorbability compared to stoichiometric HAp.

name: Fluorapatite
description: The end-member of the apatite series where fluoride replaces hydroxyl groups, increasing acid resistance.

name: Strontium-Apatite
description: Strontium-substituted hydroxyapatite used for treating osteoporosis and enhancing bone formation.

name: Chlorapatite
description: Rare apatite mineral where chloride replaces hydroxyl groups.

name: Biological Hydroxyapatite (Mature Enamel)
description: Highly oriented biological hydroxyapatite constituting mammalian dental enamel. Features unique anisotropic crystallite growth (elongated nanorods), trace fluoride/carbonate incorporations, and exceptional mechanical hardness. XRD patterns typically exhibit pronounced preferred orientation effects.

name: Magnesium-Doped HAp
description: Hydroxyapatite where a fraction of calcium is replaced by magnesium, reflecting the composition of early-stage mineralization in bone.

name: Silicon-substituted HAp
description: Silicate ions substitute for phosphate groups to enhance the bioactivity and bone bonding rate of hydroxyapatite.

name: Amorphous Calcium Phosphate
description: A non-crystalline precursor to hydroxyapatite. XRD pattern shows a broad "halo" rather than sharp peaks, characteristic of amorphous states.

name: Biological Hydroxyapatite (Dentin Matrix)
description: Nanocrystalline biological hydroxyapatite embedded within a collagenous matrix, characteristic of mammalian dentin and mature trabecular bone. Exhibits extensive ionic substitutions, very small domain sizes, and broad diffraction profiles indicative of high specific surface area.

name: Lead-doped HAp
description: Hydroxyapatite used for heavy metal remediation. Lead ions substitute for calcium, significantly shifting lattice parameters.

name: Cadmium-doped HAp
description: Apatite structure containing cadmium, often studied in the context of toxic metal uptake from the environment.

name: Magnetite (Hyperthermia)
description: Superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (SPIONs) used for magnetic fluid hyperthermia.

name: Cobalt Ferrite
description: High magnetocrystalline anisotropy ferrite, used to increase the heating efficiency in hyperthermia.

name: Maghemite
description: The fully oxidized form of magnetite, often the active phase in clinical hyperthermia agents.

name: Zinc-doped Ferrite
description: Zinc-substituted magnetite spinel ferrite (Zn0.5Fe2.5O4) where non-magnetic Zn²⁺ preferentially occupies tetrahedral A-sites, raising room-temperature saturation magnetization and lowering Curie temperature for soft magnetic cores and biomedical hyperthermia. Cubic Fd-3m (No. 227), a = 8.420 Å, Z = 8.

name: Zinc Oxide (ZnO)
description: Hexagonal wurtzite zincite (ZnO), a direct wide-bandgap (3.37 eV) piezoelectric semiconductor and NIST SRM 674b quantitative XRD reference material. Used in varistors, transparent conducting oxides (AZO), photocatalysis, UV optoelectronics, and rubber vulcanization. Hexagonal P63mc (No. 186), a = 3.2498 Å, c = 5.2066 Å, Z = 2, PDF 00-036-1451.

name: Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE)
description: A synthetic fluoropolymer of tetrafluoroethylene.

name: Polyethylene (HDPE)
description: High-density polyethylene, a versatile thermoplastic polymer.

name: Polypropylene (iPP)
description: Isotactic polypropylene, alpha-form semi-crystalline structure.

name: Nylon 6 (Polyamide)
description: A semi-crystalline polyamide synthesized via ring-opening polymerization.

name: Quartz (SiO2)
description: A hard, crystalline mineral composed of silica (silicon dioxide).

name: Halite (NaCl)
description: Commonly known as rock salt, it is the mineral form of sodium chloride.

name: Sylvite (KCl)
description: Potassium chloride is a metal halide salt composed of potassium and chlorine.

name: Hematite (Fe2O3)
description: One of the most abundant minerals on Earth's surface and an important ore of iron.

name: Aluminum (Al)
description: A silvery-white, soft, non-magnetic and ductile metal.

name: Copper (Cu)
description: A soft, malleable, and ductile metal with very high thermal and electrical conductivity.

name: Magnesium Oxide (MgO)
description: Periclase cubic rock-salt magnesium oxide (MgO) with an exceptionally high melting point (2852 °C), wide optical bandgap (7.8 eV), and superior thermal shock resistance. Standard basic refractory lining, spintronic MTJ tunnel barrier, and electrical heating insulator. Cubic Fm-3m (No. 225), a = 4.2112 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-045-0946.

name: Titanium (Ti)
description: A lustrous transition metal with a silver color, low density, and high strength.

name: Cerium Oxide (CeO2)
description: A pale yellow-white powder, highly used as a catalyst and in glass polishing.

name: Calcite (CaCO3)
description: A carbonate mineral and the most stable polymorph of calcium carbonate.

name: Tungsten (W)
description: A rare metal known for its robustness and the highest melting point of all elements.

name: Diamond (C)
description: The hardest natural material known, a metastable allotrope of carbon.

name: Corundum (Al2O3)
description: Thermodynamically stable alpha-alumina (α-Al2O3, Corundum) with hexagonal close-packed (ABAB) oxygen sublattice and Al3+ occupying 2/3 of octahedral interstices. Trigonal R-3c (No. 167), a = 4.7589 Å, c = 12.9917 Å, Z = 6, PDF 00-046-1212. Forms irreversibly above ~1050–1200 °C from all transition aluminas.

name: Gamma-Alumina (γ-Al2O3)
description: Cubic defect-spinel transition alumina (FCC ABCABC oxygen sublattice with Al vacancies) formed by thermal dehydration of boehmite (γ-AlOOH) at 450–750 °C. Cubic Fd-3m (No. 227), a = 7.911 Å, PDF 00-010-0425. High specific surface area (150–300 m²/g) prized for heterogeneous catalysis and adsorption.

name: Eta-Alumina (η-Al2O3)
description: Cubic defect-spinel transition alumina derived from thermal decomposition of bayerite (α-Al(OH)3) at 250–500 °C (pathway: Bayerite → η → θ → α). Cubic Fd-3m (No. 227), a = 7.906 Å, PDF 00-004-0875. Exhibits higher (111) stacking-fault disorder and stronger surface Lewis acidity than γ-Al2O3.

name: Delta-Alumina (δ-Al2O3, Tetragonal)
description: Tetragonal cation-vacancy-ordered spinel superstructure of γ-Al2O3 formed by calcination at 750–950 °C (c ≈ 3a_spinel). Tetragonal P-4m2 (No. 115), a = 7.963 Å, c = 23.470 Å, PDF 00-046-1131. Characteristic doublet splitting of the 45.5°/46.4° and 66.4°/67.0° spinel reflections.

name: Delta-Prime Alumina (δ*-Al2O3, Orthorhombic)
description: Orthorhombic superlattice polymorph of delta-alumina (δ*-Al2O3) formed during rapid solidification of molten alumina droplets or boehmite calcination around 800–950 °C. Orthorhombic P212121 (No. 19), a = 7.934 Å, b = 7.956 Å, c = 11.711 Å (c ≈ 1.5a_spinel), PDF 00-046-1215.

name: Theta-Alumina (θ-Al2O3)
description: High-temperature monoclinic transition alumina (isostructural with β-Ga2O3) forming between 850 and 1100 °C immediately prior to the reconstructive θ → α-Al2O3 transformation. Monoclinic C2/m (No. 12), a = 11.795 Å, b = 2.910 Å, c = 5.621 Å, β = 103.79°, Z = 4, PDF 00-035-0121. Half of Al3+ occupy tetrahedral sites and half octahedral sites.

name: Kappa-Alumina (κ-Al2O3)
description: Metastable orthorhombic alumina polymorph with ABAC close-packed oxygen stacking (75% octahedral, 25% tetrahedral Al3+) synthesized via CVD wear coatings or calcination of gibbsite/tohdite (Gibbsite → χ → κ → α at 750–1050 °C). Orthorhombic Pna21 (No. 33), a = 4.835 Å, b = 8.311 Å, c = 8.936 Å, Z = 8, PDF 00-052-0803.

name: Chi-Alumina (χ-Al2O3)
description: Hexagonal transition alumina produced by thermal dehydration of gibbsite (γ-Al(OH)3) in air at 300–750 °C (Gibbsite → χ → κ → α) with disordered layered ABAC/ABAB oxygen packing. Hexagonal P6/mmm (No. 191), a = 5.560 Å, c = 13.440 Å, PDF 00-013-0373.

name: Lambda-Alumina (λ-Al2O3)
description: Rare monoclinic metastable alumina polymorph obtained by oxidative decomposition of β-AlH3 or high-temperature treatment of ammonium aluminum carbonate hydroxide. Monoclinic P21/c (No. 14), a = 7.630 Å, b = 10.200 Å, c = 9.090 Å, β = 94.50°.

name: Iota-Alumina (ι-Al2O3)
description: Orthorhombic mullite-type (silica-free Al2O3) metastable polymorph obtained by rapid quenching of alumina melts or devitrification of amorphous Al2O3 films. Orthorhombic Pbam (No. 55), a = 7.590 Å, b = 7.670 Å, c = 2.875 Å, PDF 00-012-0539.

name: Rho-Alumina (ρ-Al2O3, Amorphous)
description: X-ray amorphous / poorly ordered transition alumina formed by vacuum dehydration or flash calcination of gibbsite at 200–450 °C (Gibbsite → ρ → η → θ → α). Displays broad diffuse scattering halos centered near 37.5° and 67.0° 2θ and uniquely rehydrates in water to form bayerite/boehmite.

name: Beta-Alumina (β-Al2O3, NaAl11O17)
description: Layered two-block hexagonal sodium polyaluminate (NaAl11O17, two spinel blocks separated by mirror conduction planes along c) exhibiting rapid 2D Na+ superionic conductivity. Hexagonal P63/mmc (No. 194), a = 5.594 Å, c = 22.530 Å, Z = 2, PDF 00-031-1263.

name: Beta-Double-Prime Alumina (β''-Al2O3, Na1.67Al10.33O17)
description: Rhombohedral three-block sodium polyaluminate superionic conductor (Na1.67Al10.33O17, typically Mg2+ or Li+ stabilized) with ~5× higher Na+ conductivity than hexagonal β-Al2O3. Trigonal R-3m (No. 166), a = 5.600 Å, c = 33.850 Å, Z = 3, PDF 00-021-1096.

name: High-Pressure Alumina (Rh2O3(II)-type Al2O3)
description: High-pressure orthorhombic polymorph of Al2O3 adopting the Rh2O3(II) structure above ~80–100 GPa at lower-mantle conditions. Orthorhombic Pbcn (No. 60), a = 7.040 Å, b = 4.920 Å, c = 4.790 Å, Z = 4.

name: Post-Perovskite Alumina (CaIrO3-type Al2O3)
description: Ultra-high-pressure layered orthorhombic CaIrO3-type (post-perovskite) polymorph of Al2O3 stable above ~130 GPa and relevant to Earth's D'' core-mantle boundary layer. Orthorhombic Cmcm (No. 63), a = 2.660 Å, b = 8.480 Å, c = 6.460 Å, Z = 4.

name: Gibbsite (γ-Al(OH)3, Alumina Precursor)
description: Primary aluminum trihydroxide mineral (Bayer-process hydrate) and key precursor to transition aluminas (Gibbsite → χ → κ → α in air; Gibbsite → Boehmite → γ → δ → θ → α hydrothermally). Monoclinic P21/n (No. 14), a = 8.684 Å, b = 5.078 Å, c = 9.736 Å, β = 94.54°, Z = 8, PDF 00-033-0018.

name: Bayerite (α-Al(OH)3, Alumina Precursor)
description: Monoclinic polymorph of aluminum trihydroxide with ABAB hydroxyl sheet stacking; canonical precursor to η-Al2O3 upon calcination (Bayerite → η → θ → α). Monoclinic P21/a (No. 14), a = 5.062 Å, b = 8.671 Å, c = 4.713 Å, β = 90.27°, Z = 4, PDF 00-020-0011.

name: Boehmite (γ-AlO(OH), Alumina Precursor)
description: Layered orthorhombic aluminum oxyhydroxide (γ-AlO(OH)) and principal industrial precursor to γ-Al2O3 (Boehmite → γ → δ → θ → α). Orthorhombic Cmcm (No. 63), a = 3.700 Å, b = 12.227 Å, c = 2.868 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-021-1307.

name: Diaspore (α-AlO(OH), Direct α-Al2O3 Precursor)
description: Dense orthorhombic aluminum oxyhydroxide (α-AlO(OH)) with HCP oxygen packing that transforms topotactically and directly into α-Al2O3 (Corundum) at ~450–550 °C without intermediate transition phases. Orthorhombic Pbnm (No. 62), a = 4.401 Å, b = 9.425 Å, c = 2.845 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-005-0355.

name: Rutile (TiO2)
description: The most common natural form of TiO2, a major ore of titanium.

name: Anatase (TiO2)
description: A metastable mineral form of titanium dioxide.

name: Barium Titanate (BaTiO3)
description: A dielectric ceramic used for its high dielectric constant and piezoelectric properties.

name: Molybdenum Disulfide (MoS2)
description: A layered transition metal dichalcogenide used as a dry lubricant and in nanoelectronics.

name: Lead Titanate (PbTiO3)
description: A yellow solid that is insoluble in water. It is a classic ferroelectric material.

name: Zeolite A (LTA)
description: A synthetic zeolite with a pore size of about 4 Ångströms.

name: Silver (Ag)
description: A lustrous, white, soft, very ductile, and malleable transition metal.

name: Yttrium Aluminum Garnet (YAG)
description: A synthetic crystalline material of the garnet group.

name: Strontium Titanate (SrTiO3)
description: An oxide of strontium and titanium. It is a centrosymmetric cubic perovskite.

name: Lithium Iron Phosphate (LiFePO4)
description: An olivine-structured compound used as a cathode material for LIBs.

name: Gallium Nitride (GaN)
description: A binary III/V direct bandgap semiconductor commonly used in bright light-emitting diodes.

name: Gold (Au)
description: A transition metal and a group 11 element. It is one of the least reactive chemical elements.

name: Iron - Alpha (Fe)
description: The BCC allotrope of iron, stable at room temperature.

name: Graphite
description: A crystalline form of the element carbon with its atoms arranged in a hexagonal structure.

name: Calcium Fluoride (CaF2)
description: The mineral fluorite, used extensively in optics due to its wide transparency range.

name: Nickel (Ni)
description: A silvery-white lustrous metal with a slight golden tinge. It is hard and ductile.

name: Tungsten Carbide (WC)
description: An extremely hard chemical compound containing tungsten and carbon atoms.

name: Magnetite (Fe3O4)
description: A rock-forming mineral and one of the main iron ores, one of the oxides of iron.

name: Methylammonium Lead Iodide (MAPbI3)
description: A primary material used in high-efficiency perovskite solar cells.

name: Silicon Carbide (SiC)
description: A hard chemical compound of silicon and carbon. Moissanite is its rare mineral form.

name: Gallium Arsenide (GaAs)
description: A III-V direct bandgap semiconductor used in integrated circuits and solar cells.

name: Bismuth Ferrite (BiFeO3)
description: One of the few multiferroic materials that is both ferroelectric and antiferromagnetic at room temp.

name: Indium Tin Oxide (ITO)
description: A ternary composition of indium, tin and oxygen. It is transparent and conductive.

name: Pyrite (FeS2)
description: Known as fool's gold, it is an iron sulfide mineral.

name: Chromium (Cr)
description: Room-temperature body-centered cubic (α-Cr) transition metal characterized by high hardness, corrosion-passivating Cr2O3 surface film, and antiferromagnetic Néel ordering below 311 K. Cubic Im-3m (No. 229), a = 2.8839 Å, Z = 2, PDF 00-006-0694.

name: Gallium Oxide (Ga2O3)
description: An inorganic compound and ultra-wide-bandgap semiconductor.

name: Cadmium Telluride (CdTe)
description: A crystalline compound used as an infrared optical window and a solar cell material.

name: Bismuth Telluride (Bi2Te3)
description: A gray powder that is a compound of bismuth and tellurium. It is a semiconductor and thermoelectric material.

name: Tin Oxide (SnO2)
description: The mineral cassiterite, the main ore of tin. Used as a gas sensor material.

name: Lithium Cobalt Oxide (LiCoO2)
description: A chemical compound used as a positive electrode in lithium-ion batteries.

name: Silicon Nitride (Si3N4)
description: A hard, solid ceramic used in high-strength and high-temperature applications.

name: Aluminum Nitride (AlN)
description: A technical ceramic with an unusual combination of high thermal conductivity and electrical insulation.

name: Boron Nitride (h-BN)
description: Often referred to as "white graphite" because of its lubricity and hexagonal structure.

name: Gallium Phosphide (GaP)
description: A phosphide of gallium, an indirect bandgap semiconductor used in some LED devices.

name: Zinc Selenide (ZnSe)
description: Cubic zinc-blende II-VI semiconductor (Eg = 2.70 eV) prized for ultra-low absorption across 0.6–20 μm, making it the premier CO2 laser optics, FLIR thermal imaging window, and ATR-FTIR crystal. Cubic F-43m (No. 216), a = 5.6688 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-037-1463.

name: Tantalum (Ta)
description: A rare, hard, blue-gray, lustrous transition metal that is highly corrosion-resistant.

name: Vanadium Pentoxide (V2O5)
description: The chemical compound with the formula V2O5. It is a poisonous yellow/orange solid.

name: Silver Chloride (AgCl)
description: A chemical compound with the chemical formula AgCl. It occurs naturally as the mineral chlorargyrite.

name: Manganese Oxide (MnO2)
description: The inorganic compound with the formula MnO2, also known as pyrolusite.

name: Nickel Oxide (NiO)
description: The mineral bunsenite, an antiferromagnetic semiconductor.

name: Cobalt(II,III) Oxide (Co3O4)
description: Black antiferromagnetic solid, a mixed-valence compound containing both Co(II) and Co(III).

name: Lead Zirconate Titanate (PZT)
description: A ceramic perovskite material that shows a marked piezoelectric effect.

name: Barium Ferrite (BaFe12O19)
description: A highly magnetic material, also called barium hexaferrite.

name: Vanadium Dioxide (VO2)
description: Known for its reversible metal-insulator transition at 68°C.

name: Tungsten Trioxide (WO3)
description: A transition metal oxide used for its electrochromic and gas sensing properties.

name: Austenite (γ-Fe)
description: The FCC allotrope of iron, typically stable above 912°C or in stainless steels.

name: Silver(I) Oxide (Ag2O)
description: A chemical compound used in silver-oxide batteries.

name: Copper(II) Oxide (CuO)
description: The mineral tenorite, a black solid and p-type semiconductor.

name: Zinc Sulfide (ZnS)
description: Low-temperature cubic zinc blende (sphalerite, β-ZnS) polymorph, primary zinc ore mineral and wide-bandgap (3.68 eV) infrared-transparent optical window and electroluminescent phosphor host. Cubic F-43m (No. 216), a = 5.4093 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-005-0566.

name: beta-Tricalcium Phosphate (beta-TCP)
description: Low-temperature whitlockite-type rhombohedral polymorph of tricalcium phosphate (β-Ca3(PO4)2, Ca/P = 1.50), thermodynamically stable up to 1125 °C; premier bioresorbable osteoconductive bone-graft ceramic. Rhombohedral (Trigonal) R3c (No. 161), a = 10.4352 Å, c = 37.4029 Å, Z = 21, PDF 00-009-0169.

name: Bioactive Glass (45S5)
description: A glass-ceramic material that bonds to both bone and soft tissue.

name: Bioactive Glass (13-93)
description: A more silicate-rich bioactive glass compared to 45S5, often used for scaffolds and slow-resorption implants.

name: Bioactive Glass (S53P4)
description: A dedicated clinical grade bioglass with potent antibacterial properties.

name: Brushite (DCPD)
description: Dicalcium phosphate dihydrate, a precursor to hydroxyapatite in biological systems.

name: Monetite (DCP)
description: Anhydrous dicalcium phosphate, used in calcium phosphate cements.

name: Bio-Aragonite
description: A calcium carbonate polymorph found in nacre and mollusk shells.

name: Tetracalcium Phosphate (TTCP)
description: The most basic calcium phosphate, often used in self-setting cements.

name: alpha-Tricalcium Phosphate (alpha-TCP)
description: High-temperature monoclinic polymorph of tricalcium phosphate (α-Ca3(PO4)2, stable 1125–1430 °C and retained metastably at room temperature by quenching); rapidly hydrolyzes in physiological fluids to calcium-deficient hydroxyapatite (CDHA) for self-setting bone cements. Monoclinic P21/a (No. 14), a = 12.887 Å, b = 27.280 Å, c = 15.219 Å, β = 126.20°, Z = 24, PDF 00-029-0359.

name: Lithium Titanate (Li4Ti5O12)
description: An "extremely safe" anode material for lithium-ion batteries with zero-strain characteristics.

name: YBCO Superconductor (YBa2Cu3O7)
description: The first material found to become a superconductor above the boiling point of liquid nitrogen.

name: Zeolite ZSM-5
description: A high-silica zeolite used extensively in the petroleum industry as a heterogeneous catalyst.

name: Metal-Organic Framework-5 (MOF-5)
description: A prototypical metal-organic framework with exceptionally high surface area for gas storage.

name: Platinum (Pt)
description: A dense, malleable, ductile, highly unreactive precious metal.

name: Palladium (Pd)
description: A shiny, silvery-white metal that has the lowest melting point and is the least dense of the PGMs.

name: NMC-111 (LiNi1/3Mn1/3Co1/3O2)
description: A mixed metal oxide used as a cathode material in state-of-the-art Li-ion batteries.

name: Yttria-Stabilized Zirconia (YSZ)
description: Zirconium dioxide stabilized with 8 mol% yttria, an ideal electrolyte for solid oxide fuel cells.

name: Strontium Ruthenate (SrRuO3)
description: A metallic ferromagnet with high chemical stability and excellent lattice match for perovskite oxides.

name: Graphene Oxide (GO)
description: A carbon material derived from graphite with hydrophilic oxygen-containing groups.

name: Octacalcium Phosphate (OCP)
description: A transient intermediate in bone and tooth formation, structurally similar to hydroxyapatite.

name: Cellulose (Type Ib)
description: The most abundant natural polymer, forming structural components of plant cell walls.

name: Chitosan
description: A linear polysaccharide derived from chitin, exhibiting excellent biocompatibility and antimicrobial properties.

name: Silk Fibroin (Beta-Sheet)
description: The structural protein in silk, forming crystalline beta-sheet regions responsible for its high tensile strength.

name: Calcium Oxalate Monohydrate
description: Whewellite, the primary crystalline component found in most human kidney stones.

name: Amorphous Calcium Phosphate (ACP)
description: A non-crystalline phase of calcium phosphate, the initial solid phase that precipitates from high supersaturation.

name: Polylactic Acid (PLA)
description: A biodegradable and bioactive thermoplastic aliphatic polyester derived from renewable resources.

name: Polyether ether ketone (PEEK)
description: A versatile high-performance semicrystalline engineering thermoplastic used extensively in medical and space applications.

name: Collagen Type I
description: The most abundant collagen of the human body, serving as a key structural fiber in tendons, bone, and skin.

name: Uranium Dioxide (UO2)
description: Fluorite-type uranium dioxide (UO2), the primary ceramic nuclear fuel in light-water reactors. Cubic Fm-3m (No. 225), a = 5.4704 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-041-1422.

name: Thorium Dioxide (ThO2)
description: Crystalline fluorite-type thorium dioxide (thoria, ThO2), a fertile nuclear ceramic with the highest melting point of all binary oxides (3390 °C). Cubic Fm-3m (No. 225), a = 5.5974 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-042-1462.

name: Boron Carbide (B4C)
description: An extremely hard boron-carbon ceramic used in tank armor, bulletproof vests, and notably as control rods in nuclear reactors for neutron absorption.

name: Gadolinium Oxide (Gd2O3)
description: A chemical compound used as a neutron-absorbing "burnable poison" in nuclear fuel to manage reactivity over time.

name: Plutonium Dioxide (PuO2)
description: Stable fluorite-structured ceramic plutonium dioxide (PuO2) used in Mixed Oxide (MOX) nuclear fuel and deep-space radioisotope thermoelectric generators (RTGs). Cubic Fm-3m (No. 225), a = 5.3960 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-041-1170.

name: Lead (Pb)
description: A dense, soft, malleable post-transition metal used extensively for radiation shielding due to its high atomic number and density.

name: Zirconium Hydride (ZrH2)
description: A metallic hydride used as a moderator and fuel component in specialty reactors like TRIGA.

name: Beryllium Oxide (BeO)
description: An inorganic compound with high thermal conductivity and low neutron capture cross-section, used as a neutron reflector.

name: Martensite (α'-Fe)
description: A very hard, supersaturated solid solution of carbon in iron. Characterized by a body-centered tetragonal (BCT) structure formed by rapid quenching.

name: Cementite (Fe3C)
description: An intermetallic compound of iron and carbon. Hard and brittle, it is a key constituent in most steels and cast irons.

name: Titanium-6Al-4V (α+β)
description: The most common titanium alloy. Consists of a dual-phase microstructure of alpha and beta phases, offering high strength and corrosion resistance.

name: Zircaloy-4
description: Nickel-free zirconium nuclear fuel cladding alloy (Zr-1.5Sn-0.21Fe-0.11Cr, UNS R60804) for pressurized water reactors (PWR), engineered for ultra-low thermal neutron absorption cross-section and reduced hydrogen pickup compared to Zircaloy-2. Hexagonal P63/mmc (No. 194), a = 3.231 Å, c = 5.149 Å, Z = 2.

name: Nuclear Graphite
description: Highly purified graphite optimized for its high moderating ratio and structural stability under intense radiation.

name: Neodymium Magnet (Nd2Fe14B)
description: The strongest type of permanent magnet commercially available, featuring high coercivity and magnetic remanence.

name: Titanium Carbide (TiC)
description: An extremely hard refractory ceramic material, similar to tungsten carbide.

name: Chromium(III) Oxide (Cr2O3)
description: Eskolaite, a hard green mineral used as a pigment and for polishing.

name: Cobalt Ferrite (CoFe2O4)
description: A hard magnetic material with high coercivity and moderate saturation magnetization.

name: Bismuth Oxychloride (BiOCl)
description: A layered material with excellent light-harvesting and photocatalytic properties.

name: Cesium Lead Iodide (CsPbI3)
description: An all-inorganic perovskite material with high thermal stability for solar cells.

name: Titanium MXene (Ti3C2Tx)
description: A prominent member of the MXene family of two-dimensional transition metal carbides.

name: UiO-66 (Zr-MOF)
description: A highly stable zirconium-based MOF with exceptional chemical and thermal resistance.

name: HKUST-1 (Cu-MOF)
description: A well-known copper-based MOF with high surface area and open metal sites.

name: Molybdenum Trioxide (MoO3)
description: An n-type semiconductor used in electrochromic devices and catalysis.

name: Vanadium(III) Oxide (V2O3)
description: A classic Mott insulator that undergoes a metal-insulator transition around 150 K.

name: Perovskite (CaTiO3)
description: The namesake of the perovskite crystal structure, found in the Earth's mantle.

name: Feldspar (Orthoclase)
description: A common rock-forming tectosilicate mineral.

name: Stainless Steel 316L
description: Low-carbon FCC austenitic steel with excellent corrosion resistance containing Mo.

name: Stainless Steel 304
description: The most common austenitic stainless steel, widely used in various industries.

name: Stainless Steel 310
description: Heat-resistant austenitic stainless steel with high chromium and nickel content.

name: Stainless Steel 430
description: Ferritic stainless steel (BCC) with good corrosion resistance and formability.

name: Ti-6Al-4V (Grade 5)
description: High-strength alpha-beta titanium alloy, widely used in aerospace and medical implants.

name: Brass (C26000)
description: Single-phase FCC alpha-brass (Cartridge Brass C26000, Cu-30wt%Zn) with substantial lattice expansion relative to pure Cu (a = 3.6810 vs 3.6150 Å) due to substitutional Zn dissolution. Optimal combination of high ductility, cold-drawing workability, and corrosion resistance. Cubic Fm-3m (No. 225), a = 3.6810 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-050-1333.

name: Inconel 718
description: Nickel-chromium-based superalloy used for high-temperature applications.

name: Stainless Steel 17-4PH
description: Precipitation-hardening martensitic stainless steel with high strength and high corrosion resistance.

name: Duplex Stainless Steel 2205
description: A nitrogen-enhanced duplex stainless steel designed to combat common corrosion problems, combining FCC and BCC phases.

name: Hastelloy C-276
description: Nickel-molybdenum-chromium-tungsten superalloy with outstanding pitting and crevice corrosion resistance.

name: Tool Steel H13
description: Chromium-molybdenum hot work tool steel exhibiting outstanding resistance to thermal fatigue cracking.

name: FeCrAl Alloy (Kanthal APM)
description: An advanced powder metallurgically produced FeCrAl alloy with excellent form-stability and high-temperature oxidation resistance.

name: High-Entropy Alloy (AlCoCrFeNi)
description: Equiatomic multi-principal-element alloy exhibiting outstanding blend of high strength, ductility, and high-temperature stability.

name: SBA-15 (Mesoporous Silica)
description: Hexagonal mesoporous silica with high surface area and thick walls.

name: MCM-41 (Mesoporous Silica)
description: Ordered mesoporous material with high pore volume and surface area.

name: MOF-5 (Zinc Tera-terephthalate)
description: Classic Metal-Organic Framework with high porosity for gas storage and drug delivery.

name: ZIF-8 (Zeolitic Imidazolate Framework)
description: Chemically stable MOF used for pH-responsive drug delivery.

name: Caffeine (Anhydrous)
description: A commonly used CNS stimulant. The anhydrous form is mostly used in pharmaceuticals. It exists in two polymorphs, alpha (high temp) and beta (room temp).

name: Ascorbic Acid (Vitamin C)
description: L-ascorbic acid. A water-soluble vitamin and powerful antioxidant. Used conventionally as a dietary supplement and in cosmetic formulations.

name: Sucrose (Sugar)
description: Common table sugar. Widely used as a pharmaceutical excipient (filler, binder, or coating agent) and in food industries.

name: Cholesterol
description: A major structural component of the cell membranes and a precursor to steroid hormones. Often found in gallstones forming characteristic platelike crystals.

name: Carbamazepine (Form III)
description: An anticonvulsant and mood-stabilizing drug. Form III is the most stable polymorph at room temperature.

name: Theophylline (Anhydrous)
description: A methylxanthine drug used in therapy for respiratory diseases. Highly prone to form hydrates, so anhydrous phase verification is critical.

name: Naproxen (S-Naproxen)
description: A widely used NSAID (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug). Typically the pure S-enantiomer is supplied.

name: Ibuprofen (Crystalline)
description: Propionic acid derivative drug, showing sharp Bragg peaks in its crystalline form.

name: Paracetamol (Acetaminophen)
description: Common analgesic. Studied for polymorphic transitions in drug formulation.

name: Polyethylene (PE)
description: Semicrystalline thermoplastic showing characteristic orthorhombic crystalline peaks.

name: YBCO Superconductor
description: High-temperature superconducting ceramic material (Yttrium Barium Copper Oxide).

name: Portland Cement (Alite)
description: The primary active phase (Tricalcium Silicate) in Portland cement clinker.

name: Graphene (C)
description: A single layer of carbon atoms arranged in a two-dimensional honeycomb lattice.

name: Lithium Manganese Oxide (LiMn2O4)
description: Spinel-structured oxide used as a cathode material in lithium-ion batteries.

name: Bismuth (Bi)
description: A brittle metal with a pinkish tinge, known for its remarkably low thermal conductivity and high diamagnetism.

name: Germanium (Ge)
description: A lustrous, hard, grayish-white metalloid in the carbon group, used historically in early transistors.

name: Titanium Nitride (TiN)
description: An extremely hard ceramic material, often used as a coating to improve surface properties.

name: Molybdenum (Mo)
description: A refractory metal used in high-strength alloys and high-temperature applications.

name: Iridium (Ir)
description: A very hard, brittle, silvery-white transition metal of the platinum group.

name: Osmium (Os)
description: The densest naturally occurring element, a hard, brittle, bluish-white transition metal.

name: Rhodium (Rh)
description: A rare, silvery-white, hard, corrosion-resistant transition metal.

name: Lithium Tantalate (LiTaO3)
description: A piezoelectric and ferroelectric material highly useful in nonlinear optics and surface acoustic wave devices.

name: Lithium Niobate (LiNbO3)
description: A colorless solid, known for its optical properties including the linear electro-optic effect.

name: Lead Sulphide (PbS)
description: Known as galena, a narrow bandgap semiconductor used in infrared detectors.

name: Zinc Telluride (ZnTe)
description: Direct-bandgap (2.26 eV) cubic zinc-blende II-VI semiconductor widely used for electro-optic terahertz (THz) generation/detection crystals, CdTe solar cell back-contacts, and green LEDs. Cubic F-43m (No. 216), a = 6.1026 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-015-0746.

name: Lanthanum Aluminate (LaAlO3)
description: A synthetic ceramic oxide that is widely used as a high-quality substrate for epitaxial growth of thin films.

name: Cuprite (Cu2O)
description: A copper oxide mineral that naturally crystallizes as an octahedral cubic structure and acts as a p-type semiconductor.

name: Cadmium Selenide (CdSe)
description: A binary solid semiconductor known for its highly tunable optical properties when structured as colloidal quantum dots.

name: Silicon Monoxide (SiO)
description: An amorphous Silicon compound favored for lithium battery anodes due to high capacity and minimized swelling compared to pure Silicon.

name: Yttrium Oxide (Y2O3)
description: An air-stable white solid refractory substance, widely used in optics and host materials for phosphors.

name: Barium Zirconate (BaZrO3)
description: A high melting point ceramic possessing high protonic conductivity, ideal for solid oxide fuel cell membranes.

name: NASICON (Na3Zr2Si2PO12)
description: Sodium Super Ionic Conductor with high ionic conductivity at room temperature, crucial for standard solid state Sodium battering systems.

name: Titanium Disulfide (TiS2)
description: A layered transition metal dichalcogenide compound with a high electrical conductivity and excellent intercalation chemistry.

name: Hafnium Oxide (HfO2)
description: A high-k dielectric material used as gate oxides in modern computer processors and dynamic random-access memory (DRAM).

name: Lead-Free Solder (SAC305)
description: An alloy composed of Tin, Silver, and Copper (Sn-Ag-Cu), widely used as solder for computer hardware printed circuit boards.

name: Tantalum Pentoxide (Ta2O5)
description: A high refractive index and high dielectric constant material used in motherboard decoupler capacitors.

name: Single-Walled Carbon Nanotubes (SWCNTs)
description: Seamless cylinders of graphene sheets demonstrating ballistical electron conductivity, studied as channels for sub-3nm transistors.

name: Black Phosphorus (Phosphorene)
description: An anisotropic layered elemental 2D semiconductor possessing a direct bandgap and exceptionally high charge-carrier mobility.

name: Indium Gallium Zinc Oxide (IGZO)
description: An amorphous or highly textured oxide semiconductor used primarily as the active channel material of thin-film transistors (TFTs) in OLED/LCD displays.

name: Superparamagnetic Iron Oxide Nanoparticles (SPIONs)
description: Biocompatible magnetite/maghemite core nanoparticles used as T2 MRI contrast enhancement agents and in target-guided magnetic hyperthermia cancer therapy.

name: Mesoporous Silica Nanoparticles (MSN / MCM-41)
description: A solid silicate framework featuring highly organized hexagonal arrays of mesopores, ideal for high-capacity drug loading and controlled release.

name: Silver Nanoparticles (AgNPs)
description: Ultrafine silver crystals with extremely high surface-to-volume ratio, demonstrating potent oligodynamic antimicrobic/antiviral effects.

name: Alpha-Uranium Metal
description: Room-temperature orthorhombic allotrope of elemental uranium (α-U, stable below 668 °C) with corrugated (010) atomic layers and highly anisotropic thermal expansion. Orthorhombic Cmcm (No. 63), a = 2.8537 Å, b = 5.8695 Å, c = 4.9548 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-011-0628.

name: Uranium Dioxide
description: Stoichiometric fluorite-structured uranium dioxide (UO2), the primary ceramic nuclear fuel used in commercial light-water reactors. Cubic Fm-3m (No. 225), a = 5.4704 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-041-1422.

name: Triuranium Octoxide
description: Thermodynamically most stable mixed-valence (U5+/U6+) uranium oxide (α-U3O8) in air; the primary constituent of refined yellowcake concentrate and long-term uranium oxide storage. Orthorhombic C2mm (No. 38), a = 6.716 Å, b = 11.960 Å, c = 4.147 Å, Z = 2, PDF 00-047-1493.

name: Uranium Trioxide
description: Orange-yellow gamma-uranium trioxide (γ-UO3), the most stable polymorph of hexavalent UO3 produced by denitration of uranyl nitrate in nuclear fuel conversion. Orthorhombic Fddd (No. 70), a = 9.813 Å, b = 19.930 Å, c = 9.711 Å, Z = 32, PDF 00-031-1425.

name: Silicon Carbide (6H-SiC)
description: Wide bandgap semiconductor 6H-SiC polytype. Extremely hard and heat resistant.

name: Barium Titanate (Tetragonal)
description: Tetragonal phase BaTiO3 showing characteristic peak splitting due to ferroelectric distortion.

name: Titanium (Grade 2 CP)
description: Commercially pure titanium (HCP structure). Excellent corrosion resistance and biocompatibility.

name: Magnesium Alloy (AZ31B)
description: Most widely used wrought magnesium alloy (AZ31B: Mg-3wt%Al-1wt%Zn-0.3wt%Mn). Substitutional Al and Zn solutes slightly contract the HCP α-Mg unit cell (a = 3.195 Å, c = 5.188 Å), shifting Bragg peaks ~0.15° higher than pure Mg. Rolled sheet often shows strong basal (002) texture. Hexagonal P63/mmc (No. 194), PDF 00-035-0821 (solid solution).

name: Cobalt-Chrome (CoCrMo)
description: High-strength, highly wear-resistant alloy favored for joint replacement implants.

name: Nitinol (NiTi Shape Memory)
description: Equiatomic nickel-titanium alloy known for shape memory and superelastic phenomena at low temps (martensite) and elevated temps (austenite).

name: Aluminum Alloy (7075-T6)
description: Zinc-alloyed aluminum. Excellent strength-to-weight ratio, commonly used in aircraft structural parts.

name: Zircaloy-2
description: Tin-iron-chromium-nickel zirconium alloy (Zr-1.5Sn-0.15Fe-0.10Cr-0.05Ni, UNS R60802) widely used as boiling water reactor (BWR) fuel cladding and channel boxes due to its low thermal neutron capture cross-section and high nodular corrosion resistance in oxygenated steam. Hexagonal P63/mmc (No. 194), a = 3.230 Å, c = 5.148 Å, Z = 2.

name: Hastelloy X
description: Nickel-chromium-iron-molybdenum superalloy. Outstanding high-temperature strength and oxidation resistance.

name: Monel 400
description: Nickel-copper alloy resistive to sea water and high-velocity brackish waters.

name: Maraging Steel (Grade 300)
description: Ultra-high-strength steel that is iron-based, highly alloyed with nickel. Low carbon, derives strength from intermetallic precipitates.

name: Beryllium (Be)
description: Extremely lightweight, stiff metal with exceptional specific heat and thermal conductivity.

name: Vanadium (V)
description: Hard, silvery-grey, malleable transition metal. Form stable oxides and is widely used for creating specialty steel alloys (high-speed tool steels).

name: Niobium (Nb)
description: Light grey, crystalline, and ductile transition metal. Crucial for superconducting materials and high-temp jet-engine superalloys.

name: Zirconium (Zr)
description: Room-temperature hexagonal close-packed (α-Zr) transition metal prized for its extremely low thermal neutron absorption cross-section (0.185 barn), self-healing passive ZrO2 film in mineral acids, and low magnetic susceptibility for MRI-safe implants. Hexagonal P63/mmc (No. 194), a = 3.2316 Å, c = 5.1475 Å, Z = 2, PDF 00-005-0665.

name: Magnesium (Mg)
description: Lightest structural engineering metal (1.738 g/cm³) crystallizing in a nearly ideal HCP lattice (c/a = 1.6236). Essential base phase for aerospace/automotive lightweighting alloys, bioresorbable orthopedic implants, hydrogen storage, and rechargeable magnesium batteries. Hexagonal P63/mmc (No. 194), a = 3.2094 Å, c = 5.2108 Å, Z = 2, PDF 00-035-0821.

name: Tin (Sn)
description: Silvery metal that characteristically has a faint yellow hue. The beta (white tin) phase is stable at room temperature.

name: Zinc (Zn)
description: Elemental hexagonal close-packed zinc metal with an anomalously large axial ratio (c/a = 1.856) that causes (002) at 36.29° to precede (100) at 38.99°. Widely used for hot-dip galvanizing, cathodic protection anodes, die-casting alloys, and aqueous zinc-ion battery anodes. Hexagonal P63/mmc (No. 194), a = 2.6650 Å, c = 4.9470 Å, Z = 2, PDF 00-004-0831.

name: Electrical Steel (Fe-Si)
description: Iron alloy containing up to 6.5% silicon. Tailored for specific magnetic properties like small hysteresis area and high permeability.

name: Permalloy (Ni-Fe)
description: Nickel-iron magnetic alloy (approx. 80% Ni, 20% Fe) with remarkably high magnetic permeability.

name: Bronze (Phosphor Bronze)
description: Copper alloy with 0.5-11% tin and 0.01-0.35% phosphorus. Notable for toughness, high strength and low coefficient of friction.

name: Zirconia Toughened Alumina (ZTA)
description: Composite ceramic combining a Trigonal α-Al2O3 (R-3c) matrix with dispersed Tetragonal (P42/nmc) and stress-transformable Monoclinic (P21/c) ZrO2 toughening phases. Used for high-reliability hip joint replacements and cutting inserts.

name: Y-TZP (Yttria-stabilized Zirconia)
description: Tetragonal zirconia polycrystals stabilized with yttria. High flexural strength and fracture toughness, standard for dental crowns.

name: Alginate
description: Natural biopolymer derived from brown seaweed. Widely used for hydrogel formulations and dental impressions.

name: Hyaluronic Acid (HA)
description: Glycosaminoglycan present in connective tissue, highly hydrating and used in osteoarthritis injections and cosmetics.

name: Diclofenac Sodium
description: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) taken or applied to reduce inflammation and as an analgesic reducing pain.

name: Aspirin (Acetylsalicylic Acid)
description: One of the mostly widely used medications to treat pain, fever, and inflammation, and as an antiplatelet.

name: Amoxicillin Trihydrate
description: A broad-spectrum penicillin antibiotic used to treat various bacterial infections.

name: Mg-Substituted beta-TCP (Mg-TCP)
description: Beta tricalcium phosphate doped with magnesium. Enhances osteogenesis and delays the rapid resorption rate of pure beta-TCP.

name: Sr-Substituted beta-TCP (Sr-TCP)
description: Strontium substitution shifts the lattice peaks slightly and greatly promotes osteoblast proliferation while inhibiting osteoclasts.

name: Zn-Substituted HAp (Zn-HAp)
description: Zinc doping introduces antibacterial properties into the hydroxyapatite lattice and promotes bone formation.

name: Barium Sulfate
description: Used clinically as a radiocontrast agent for X-ray imaging and other diagnostic procedures. Extremely insoluble and safe orally.

name: Polymethyl Methacrylate (PMMA)
description: Also known as bone cement. Wide amorphous halos in XRD. Used to affix implants or remodel lost bone in orthopedics.

name: Polycaprolactone (PCL)
description: Biodegradable polyester with a low melting point (~60 C). Widely used for 3D printed tissue engineering scaffolds and long-term implantable drug delivery devices.

name: Poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA)
description: A co-polymer synthesized by ring-opening co-polymerization. Tunable degradation rates make it ideal for biodegradable sutures and nano-particle drug carriers.

name: TiO2 Nanotubes (Biomedical)
description: Formed via anodization on titanium implants. Enhances osteoblast adhesion, allows localized drug delivery, and provides antibacterial properties.

name: Calcium Sulfate Hemihydrate
description: Plaster of Paris. Hardens upon wetting, resorbs relatively quickly in vivo. Used as an inexpensive bone void filler or binder.

name: Calcium Sulfate Dihydrate
description: Gypsum. The set phase of calcium sulfate void fillers.

name: Whitlockite
description: Second most abundant mineral in human bone. Magnesium-incorporated calcium phosphate. Shows superior osteogenic properties vs HAp in some studies.

name: Meloxicam
description: NSAID used to relieve pain and inflammation in rheumatic diseases and osteoarthritis.

name: Curcumin
description: Active ingredient of turmeric. Shows diverse pharmacological activities like anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and anti-cancer effects.

name: Olivine (Forsterite)
description: Magnesium end-member olivine orthosilicate (Mg2SiO4, forsterite), dominant upper-mantle mineral and high-Q microwave dielectric / bioactive bone-scaffold ceramic. Orthorhombic Pbnm (No. 62), a = 4.7540 Å, b = 10.1971 Å, c = 5.9806 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-034-0189.

name: Pyroxene (Enstatite)
description: Magnesium end-member orthopyroxene chain silicate (MgSiO3, enstatite), major Earth mantle / chondritic meteorite mineral and low-loss steatite ceramic electrical insulator. Orthorhombic Pbca (No. 61), a = 18.225 Å, b = 8.815 Å, c = 5.175 Å, Z = 16, PDF 00-019-0768.

name: Biotite
description: Dark-colored mica mineral, rich in iron and magnesium. Characterized by perfect basal cleavage.

name: Muscovite
description: Light-colored, potassium-rich mica. Excellent thermal and electrical insulator.

name: Kaolinite
description: A clay mineral, part of the group of industrial minerals. Widely used in paper and ceramic industries.

name: Montmorillonite
description: Very soft phyllosilicate group of minerals that form when they precipitate from water solution as microscopic crystals, known as clay.

name: Illite
description: Non-expanding, clay-sized, micaceous mineral. Common in sedimentary rocks and soils.

name: Dolomite
description: Ordered calcium magnesium double carbonate (CaMg(CO3)2) with alternating Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ cation layers reducing symmetry from R-3c to R-3 (diagnostic ordering reflections (101) at 22.05° and (015) at 35.35°). Major raw material for Pidgeon-process metallic Mg production and dolomitic refractories. Trigonal R-3 (No. 148), a = 4.8069 Å, c = 16.0034 Å, Z = 3, PDF 00-036-0426.

name: Aragonite
description: A carbonate mineral, one of the three most common naturally occurring crystal forms of calcium carbonate. Biogenic marine origin.

name: Ilmenite
description: A titanium-iron oxide mineral, heavily magnetic. It is the most important ore of titanium.

name: Apatite (Fluorapatite)
description: A group of phosphate minerals. Fluorapatite is the most common variety and the primary source of phosphorus.

name: Zircon
description: A nesosilicate mineral. Plays an important part in radiometric dating (U-Pb).

name: Tourmaline (Schorl)
description: A crystalline boron silicate mineral compounded with elements such as aluminium, iron, magnesium, sodium, lithium, or potassium.

name: Beryl
description: A mineral composed of beryllium aluminium cyclosilicate. Includes emerald and aquamarine.

name: Almandine (Garnet)
description: The most common kind of garnet. Deep red, transparent to translucent.

name: Fullerene (C60)
description: Carbon allotrope whose molecule consists of carbon atoms connected by single and double bonds so as to form a closed or partially closed mesh.

name: Multi-walled Carbon Nanotubes (MWCNT)
description: Multiple layers of graphite superimposed and rolled in on themselves to form a tubular shape. Shows characteristic prominent 002 peak.

name: Hard Carbon
description: Non-graphitizable carbon with a disordered, porous structure. Often used as sodium-ion or lithium-ion battery anodes.

name: Glassy Carbon
description: Non-graphitizing, non-graphitizable carbon which combines glassy and ceramic properties with those of graphite.

name: Anthracite
description: Hard, compact variety of coal that has a submetallic luster. It has the highest carbon content.

name: Zirconium Diboride (ZrB2)
description: Highly covalent refractory ceramic material with a hexagonal crystal structure. Used in hypersonic flight vehicles.

name: Hafnium Diboride (HfB2)
description: Ultra-high temperature ceramic with excellent resistance to thermal shock and oxidation. Used in ICBM reentry vehicles.

name: Titanium Diboride (TiB2)
description: Extremely hard ceramic with excellent heat conductivity and electrically conductive properties, used in impact-resistant armor.

name: Uranium Silicide (U3Si2)
description: High-uranium-density, high-thermal-conductivity accident-tolerant nuclear fuel (U3Si2) used in research reactors and ATF commercial LWR fuel concepts. Tetragonal P4/mbm (No. 127), a = 7.331 Å, c = 3.900 Å, Z = 2, PDF 00-047-1070.

name: Erbium Oxide (Er2O3)
description: Utilized as a burnable absorber in light water reactors. Its neutron absorption properties deplete smoothly.

name: Ag-In-Cd Alloy (80-15-5)
description: Silver-indium-cadmium alloy widely used for control rods in pressurized water reactors (PWRs).

name: Kevlar (PPTA)
description: Semicrystalline aramid fiber. Exhibits high tensile strength-to-weight ratio. Used in soft body armor and helmets.

name: UHMWPE (Dyneema/Spectra)
description: Ultra-high-molecular-weight polyethylene. Yields the highest impact strength of any thermoplastic. Highly effective against ballistic threats.

name: Aluminum Oxynitride (ALON)
description: Optically transparent polycrystalline ceramic. Highly impact-resistant substitute for bulletproof glass.

name: Magnesium Aluminate Spinel
description: Archetypal normal cubic spinel (MgAl2O4) combining high optical transparency from UV to mid-IR, chemical inertness, and refractory thermal shock resistance (Tm = 2135 °C) for transparent armor domes and steel-ladle refractories. Cubic Fd-3m (No. 227), a = 8.0831 Å, Z = 8, PDF 00-021-1152.

name: Samarium Oxide (Sm2O3)
description: Rare earth oxide. Samarium has a high cross-section for thermal neutrons, making it useful in reactor control rods.

name: Lead Tungstate (PbWO4)
description: Dense crystal scintillator. Excellent for detecting gamma rays and is widely used in high-energy physics calorimeters.

name: Cadmium Tungstate (CdWO4)
description: High-density, highly transparent scintillator crystal used for CT and security screening systems.

name: Zirconium Carbide (ZrC)
description: Refractory metal carbide. Sometimes used as a coating material to encapsulate TRISO nuclear fuel particles.

name: Bismuth Germanate (BGO)
description: Intrinsic scintillator. Used to detect gamma radiation in high-energy physics, aerospace, and medical imaging.

name: Sodium Iodide doped with Thallium (NaI:Tl)
description: The most widely used scintillator material. High light yield for detecting gamma rays and X-rays.

name: Polonium (Po)
description: Alpha-polonium (α-Po), the only element crystallizing in a simple cubic (primitive) lattice at standard pressure; intense alpha-emitting radioactive post-transition metal. Cubic Pm-3m (No. 221), a = 3.359 Å, Z = 1, PDF 00-004-0804.

name: Polonium Dioxide (PoO2)
description: Face-centered cubic fluorite-type polonium dioxide (PoO2, yellow low-temperature form), one of the primary characterized solid compounds of polonium. Cubic Fm-3m (No. 225), a = 5.637 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-007-0018.

name: Polonium-Beryllium (Po-Be)
description: Intermetallic/composite neutron source where alpha particles from Po-210 induce neutron emission from Beryllium via the 9Be(α,n)12C reaction.

name: Plutonium (Delta Phase)
description: Face-centered cubic delta allotrope of plutonium (δ-Pu, pure equilibrium 319–452 °C or room-temperature stabilized with Ga/Al), exhibiting anomalous negative thermal expansion and lowest density among Pu phases. Cubic Fm-3m (No. 225), a = 4.6371 Å, Z = 4, PDF 01-089-4931.

name: Plutonium (Alpha Phase)
description: Room-temperature simple monoclinic allotrope of pure plutonium (α-Pu, stable below 122 °C) with 16 atoms per unit cell and 8 crystallographically inequivalent Pu sites. Monoclinic P21/m (No. 11), a = 6.183 Å, b = 4.822 Å, c = 10.963 Å, β = 101.79°, Z = 16, PDF 01-071-8350.

name: Lead(II) Oxide (Litharge)
description: Tetragonal form of lead(II) oxide. Important industrial compound in lead-acid batteries and glass.

name: Bismuth(III) Oxide
description: Important bismuth compound used to produce bismuth glass and as an oxygen ion conductor.

name: Antimony Trioxide
description: Most important commercial compound of antimony. Widely used as a flame retardant synergist.

name: Tellurium Dioxide
description: Crucial oxide of tellurium, showing excellent acousto-optic properties.

name: Germanium Dioxide
description: An oxide of germanium, used as a precursor for metallic germanium and in wide-angle camera lenses.

name: Scandium(III) Oxide
description: Rare-earth oxide with high melting point. Used in high-intensity discharge lamps and aerospace alloys.

name: Lutetium(III) Oxide
description: Dense, white rare-earth oxide. Used to make transparent ceramics and in specialty glass.

name: Niobium Pentoxide
description: Colorless insoluble solid that is the main precursor to all other materials made of niobium.

name: Wüstite (FeO)
