name: Keratinocyte Growth Factor (KGF / FGF-7 Epithelial Standard)
description: Keratinocyte specialized growth factor 7 micro-crystals. A paracrine factor secreted specifically by fibroblasts to stimulate rapid, secure epithelial barrier repair with high tissue integrity.

name: Granulocyte-Colony Stimulating Factor (G-CSF Rec-Standard)
description: Recombinant granulocyte lineage colony-stimulating cytokine standard crystallizing as four helical-bundle chains. Mobilizes active precursor hematopoiesis stem cells from bone marrow compartments into circulating blood.

name: Erythropoietin Recombinant Standard (EPO Glycosylated Core)
description: Densely packed glycoprotein erythropoietin signaling recombinant cores crystallized under high-osmolarity precipitants. Promotes erythroid progenitor cell division to restore systemic oxygen tension.

name: Bone Morphogenetic Protein 2 (BMP-2 Active Dimer)
description: Dimeric bone morphogenetic protein-2 osteoinductive crystals. Part of the transforming beta superfamily, triggering downstream osteoblast differentiation and de novo endochondral bone formation.

name: Glial Cell Line-Derived Neurotrophic Factor (GDNF Survival Scaffold)
description: Recombinant GDNF crystalline active complexes. Powerful neurotrophic peptide that facilitates the robust rescue, development, and high-affinity transmitter reuptake of midbrain dopaminergic populations.

name: Human Gamma-D Crystallin (Lens Micro-solubility Standard)
description: Somatic beta/gamma-superfamily structural protein of the ocular lens. Crucial for maintaining transparent refractive gradients and optical density within human eye lens structures. Dissolves within highly organized micro-solubility states.

name: Human Gamma-S Crystallin (Monomeric Vitreous Standard)
description: Vitreous-associated monomeric gamma-S crystallin, packed within low-symmetry monoclinic lattices. Offers excellent thermodynamic stability against cold cataract phase-separation, preserving optical integrity.

name: Human Beta-B2 Crystallin (Refractive Homodimer Crystal)
description: Major beta-crystallin structural homodimer crystallizing elegantly in space group I2 (C2 variant). Crucial for forming cohesive oligomeric associations that avoid light-scattering phases.

name: Human Beta-A3 Crystallin (Acidic Hetero-Oligomer Core)
description: Acidic beta-A3 translation component with N-terminal extensions that regulate associations. Forms highly complex trigonal crystal lattices containing water-filled channels.

name: Avian Delta-Crystallin (Argininosuccinate Lyase Homolog)
description: A taxon-specific structural crystallin recruited from the enzyme argininosuccinate lyase in birds and reptiles. Retains enzyme structural architecture but accumulates as a high-density, beautifully transparent refractive crystal.

name: Taxon-Specific Lambda-Crystallin (Rabbit Lens Protein)
description: Mammalian lambda-crystallin homologous to 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase, harvested and crystallized directly from rabbit lens extracts. Highlights evolutionary recruiting of metabolic catalysts into optical tissues.

name: Human Alpha-A Crystallin (Small Heat Shock Chaperone Core)
description: A primary small heat-shock protein chaperone displaying highly symmetric cubic structures when crystallized. Suppresses non-specific thermal aggregation of eye proteins to maintain lifelong transparency under stress.

name: Human Alpha-B Crystallin (Stress-Induced Chaperone)
description: Widely expressed alpha-B sibling of alpha-A crystallin, showing protective oligomeric assemblies in a high-symmetry tetragonal space group. Upregulated under systemic heat and oxidative stress to buffer critical lens phases.

name: Methylammonium Lead Triiodide (MAPbI3 Orthorhombic Perovskite)
description: A hybrid organic-inorganic perovskite landmark material for high-efficiency thin-film solar cells. Exhibits highly tunable bandgaps and long carrier diffusion lengths, crystallizing in a distorted corner-sharing PbI6 octahedral framework at lower temperatures.

name: Cesium Lead Tribromide (All-Inorganic Perovskite Nanocrystals)
description: All-inorganic metal halide perovskite known for high thermal stability and bright green photoluminescence. Promising candidate for quantum dot light-emitting diodes, lasers, and scintillation detectors.

name: Formamidinium Tin Triiodide (Lead-Free Eco Perovskite)
description: A leading eco-friendly, lead-free alternative hybrid perovskite for light-harvesting. Incorporates formamidinium cations within a tin iodide octahedral network, exhibiting a narrow bandgap reaching into the near-infrared spectrum.

name: Zeolitic Imidazolate Framework 8 (ZIF-8 Gas Separation MOF)
description: A prototypical metal-organic framework comprising zinc ions coordinated to 2-methylimidazole linkers. Displays exceptionally high surface area, permanent sodalite-like porosity, and outstanding thermal stability for selective gas filtration.

name: Copper Benzene-1,3,5-Tricarboxylate (HKUST-1 Porous Storage MOF)
description: Also known as Cu-BTC or HKUST-1. A highly porous cubic copper-carboxylate coordinate network with open metal sites. Revered as an industrial-scale standard for natural gas and hydrogen gas high-density storage.

name: Zirconium Terephthalate Framework (UiO-66 Stable Carrier MOF)
description: An exceptionally robust zirconium-carboxylate metal-organic framework built of Zr6O4(OH)4 nodes and terephthalate linkers. Resists extreme temperatures, strong acids, and mechanical shearing, acting as a superb water purification matrix.

name: Bismuth Strontium Calcium Copper Oxide (BSCCO-2212 Superconductor)
description: High-temperature copper-oxide superconductor BSCCO-2212 with a critical transition temperature (Tc) around 85K. Exhibits a rich anisotropic layered perovskite-like structure that is highly flexible, making it ideal for powerful superconducting magnet wire coils.

name: Yttrium Barium Copper Oxide (YBCO-123 Superconductor)
description: The absolute classic high-temperature superconductor exhibiting Tc around 93K, surpassing the liquid nitrogen boiling temperature boundary of 77K. Composed of copper-oxygen plains separated by yttrium and barium planes.

name: Bismuth Selenide (Bi2Se3 Topological Insulator)
description: A representative topological insulator system. Exhibits insulated bulk electronic bands but hosts highly conductive, gapless Dirac-cone surface states protected by structural time-reversal symmetry.

name: Bovine Gamma-B Crystallin (Model Phase-Separation Standard)
description: Highly stable model mammalian lens crystallin. Extensively studied as a physical chemistry paradigm for protein phase separation, liquid-liquid transitions, and critical opalescence in eye lens models.

name: Squid S-III Crystallin (Cephalopod Phototransduction Analogue)
description: A taxon-specific lens crystallin evolved in cephalopods via gene duplication of glutathione S-transferase enzymes. Crystallizes as highly transparent homodimers that shape high-efficiency aquatic camera eyes.

name: Human Gamma-C Crystallin (Refractive Core Monomer)
description: Essential structural monomer contributing heavily to the high refractive index of the human nuclear lens core. Stabilized by a dense network of hydrophobic slide packing and aromatic ring interactions.

name: Human Beta-B1 Crystallin (Directing Oligomer Template)
description: The largest basic beta-crystallin subunit containing highly extended terminal arms that direct the complex assembly of heterooligomeric networks in ocular lens tissues.

name: Octopus Omega-Crystallin (Cephalopod ALDH Moonlighter)
description: A major lens constituent in octopus systems displaying high sequence homology with active aldehyde dehydrogenases. Represents a beautiful classic example of optical enzyme moonlighting.

name: Avian Epsilon-Crystallin (Active Recruited LDH Catalyst)
description: Taxon-specific structural crystallin recruited directly from active lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) in crocodiles and birds. Uniquely retains full catalytic capability while maintaining excellent visual transmissive characteristics.

name: Box Jellyfish J1-Crystallin (Primitive Vision Matrix)
description: Extremely unique target protein found in the complex rhopalia eyes of box jellyfish. Designed specifically to form three-dimensional lenses that concentrate aquatic ambient rays onto photoreceptor arrays.

name: Bovine Beta-B3 Crystallin (Thermodynamic Structural Linker)
description: High-packing basic beta-crystallin subtype. Integrates within complex ocular lenses, forming dense associations that preserve perfect ocular clarity over extended thermal cycles.

name: Polylactic-co-glycolic Acid (PLGA 50:50 Scaffold Core)
description: An incredibly versatile biodegradable copolymer of lactic and glycolic acid. Degrades via bulk hydrolysis of fragile ester linkages, providing a highly biocompatible substrate for custom osteoblast seeding.

name: Crystalline Polycaprolactone (PCL Semi-Crystalline Scaffold)
description: A slow-degrading hydrophobic polyester crystallizing cleanly in orthorhombic unit cells. Retains solid structural integrity for up to two years, enabling long-term structural shielding and direct load protection.

name: Beta-Tricalcium Phosphate (beta-TCP Resorbable Bone Mineral)
description: Highly pure osteoconductive resource that rapidly resorbs via enzymatic phagocytosis. Replaced slowly with new viable bone tissue during bone remodeling cycles, offering structural calcium reservoirs.

name: Biphasic Calcium Phosphate (BCP Syn-Bone Matrix)
description: Optimized biphasic composite of hexagonal hydroxyapatite (P63/m) and bioresorbable rhombohedral β-tricalcium phosphate (R3c) balancing permanent osteoconductive mechanical support with controlled resorption for skeletal defect repair.

name: Type-I Collagen Triple Helix (Fibrillar Hydrogel Matrix)
description: Standard mammalian structural protein that reconstitutes in-vitro into soft fibrillar hydrogels. Retains cell-binding integrin sequence cues (such as RGD) supporting rapid cell migration and growth.

name: Sodium Alginate (Guluronic Acid-Rich Hydrogel Core)
description: A marine-derived block polysaccharide that undergoes near-instant thermoreversible ionic gelation when exposed to divalent calcium solutes, preserving high cell viability.

name: Purified Chitosan Crystalline (Deacetylated Marine Scaffold)
description: Crystalline aminopolysaccharide derived from marine crustacean chitin. Inherently cationic nature binds cell membranes and activates local tissue hemostasis and inflammatory cascades.

name: Silk Fibroin Heavy Chain (Bombyx mori Beta-Sheet Crystalline)
description: Protein polymer structurally defined by extensive beta-sheet structures containing crystalline glycine-alanine repeats. Delivers ultimate mechanical toughness and minimal immunogenicity profiles.

name: Poly-L-Lactic Acid (PLLA Highly Crystalline Polymer)
description: Symmetric semicrystalline polymer that crystallizes into highly organized alpha-phase helices. Excellent mechanical toughness makes it a top choice for bone reinforcement pins and vascular stents.

name: Polyglycolic Acid (PGA Highly Packable Microfibers)
description: Rigid crystalline aliphatic polyester that displays outstanding high thermal stability. Degrades promptly compared to polylactide, making it perfect for rapid soft tissue healing supports.

name: Bioactive Glass 45S5 (Bioglass Osteo-inductive Microshards)
description: A highly reactive amorphous/nanocrystalline silicate network that easily bonds with host tissue. Formulates rich surface hydroxy-carbapatite layers upon physiological fluid interaction.

name: Anhydrous Dicalcium Phosphate (Monetite Bone Biomembrane)
description: A calcium phosphate biomineral forming triclinic platelet arrays. Resorbs via cell-mediated pathways without triggering severe acid spikes, fostering exceptional bone tissue in-growth.

name: Bovine Tendon Decellularized Elastin (Structural Elastomer)
description: An elastic biomacromolecular backbone providing highly robust, long-term flexible recoil properties. Used as a structural component for engineered vascular lumens and load-bearing tissues.

name: Crystalline Hyaluronic Acid (Synovial Joint Spacer Cores)
description: Highly purified crystalline version of natural glycosaminoglycans. Possesses dense negative charge frameworks that hold immense quantities of hydrated fluid to lubricate joint spaces.

name: Egyptian Blue (Cuprorivaite)
description: One of the first synthetic pigments, created in ancient Egypt by heating silica, copper, calcium, and soda. Extremely stable and still bright blue today.

name: Han Purple
description: A synthetic barium copper silicate pigment developed in ancient China. Used to paint the Terracotta Army. Notably, it exhibits unique quantum magnetic properties at ultralow temperatures.

name: Lead White (Hydrocerussite)
description: A toxic but highly opaque white pigment used globally from Antiquity until the 20th century. Prepared by exposing lead to vinegar and horse manure vapors.

name: Cinnabar (Vermilion)
description: The bright scarlet to brick-red ore of mercury. Used since antiquity as the pigment vermilion for murals, illuminated manuscripts, and lacquerware.

name: Lapis Lazuli (Lazurite)
description: A complex feldspathoid mineral responsible for the deep celestial blue of Lapis Lazuli. Ground to produce authentic ultramarine, Europe's most expensive Renaissance pigment.

name: Malachite (Green Copper Carbonate)
description: A green copper carbonate hydroxide mineral. Extremely popular in antiquity as a pigment and for ornamental carving in Egypt and Russia.

name: Azurite
description: A soft, deep-blue copper mineral. It was the most important blue pigment in European painting from the Middle Ages to the Renaissance, often shifting green (to malachite) over centuries.

name: Orpiment
description: A golden-yellow arsenic sulfide mineral. Used worldwide as a vibrant yellow pigment despite its high toxicity, and prominently in alchemy.

name: Realgar
description: A ruby-red arsenic sulfide. Known as 'sandaracha' in ancient Rome, used as a red pigment and poison, though it degrades to yellow pararealgar under light.

name: Mayan Blue (Palygorskite base)
description: A remarkably resilient azure pigment synthesized by pre-Columbian Mesoamerican cultures. It consists of the organic dye indigo trapped within the crystalline lattice of palygorskite clay.

name: Wootz Steel (Cementite Phase in Iron)
description: Crucible steel characterized by a pattern of bands. The bands are formed by sheets of microscopic cementite (Fe3C) particles in a pearlite matrix. The origins of legendary Damascus swords.

name: Kamacite (Meteoric Iron)
description: An alloy of iron and nickel (typically up to 7% Ni) found almost exclusively in meteorites. The earliest iron tools crafted by humanity were cold-forged from kamacite.

name: Historical Bronze (Cu-Sn Alpha solid solution)
description: Characteristic XRD profile of ancient cast bronze (approx. 10% tin). The peak positions are slightly shifted from pure copper due to lattice expansion by tin atoms.

name: Electrum (Gold-Silver Alloy)
description: A naturally occurring or artificially mixed alloy of gold and silver. Used for the earliest known metal coins in Lydia and ancient Egyptian obelisk coatings.

name: Alum (Potassium Alum)
description: Used widely in antiquity as a mordant to fix organic dyes (like Tyrian Purple or Madder) onto fabrics, making the colors fast and bright.

name: Bone Ash (Hydroxylapatite)
description: Calcined animal bone, primarily hydroxylapatite. Historically used for making cupels for assaying silver/gold, and later for creating Bone China.

name: Roman Concrete (Tobermorite binder)
description: Tobermorite is a rare calcium silicate hydrate mineral, but it formed abundantly in Roman marine concrete (opus caementicium) yielding incredible multi-millennia durability.

name: Natron
description: A naturally occurring mixture of sodium carbonate decahydrate and sodium bicarbonate. Essential in ancient Egyptian mummification and early glassmaking.

name: Litharge
description: Lead(II) oxide (red/yellow). Crucial in antiquity for the cupellation of silver, and as an historic pigment and drying agent for oil paints.

name: Verdigris (Copper Acetate)
description: A synthetic blue-green pigment widely used from antiquity to the 19th century, made by hanging copper plates over boiling vinegar in sealed pots.

name: Roman Concrete (Alberese Lime)
description: Ancient Roman marine concrete composed of quicklime, volcanic ash, and pumice. Famous for self-healing cracks through fluid chemistry.

name: Egyptian Natron
description: A naturally occurring mixture of sodium carbonate decahydrate and sodium bicarbonate, harvested from dry lake beds and heavily utilized in Egyptian mummification.

name: Corinthian Bronze
description: Highly prized alloy of classical antiquity, supposedly formed by the mixture of copper, gold, and silver. A standard metal in Ancient Greece and Rome.

name: Maya Blue
description: An incredibly durable ancient Mesoamerican pigment created by intercalating indigo dye into the clay mineral palygorskite.

name: Greek Electrum
description: A naturally occurring or historically smelted alloy of gold and silver widely used in ancient Lydia and Greece for early coinage.

name: Silicon Standard
description: Internal reference standard used globally for peak position and line-broadening calibration.

name: Lanthanum Hexaboride (LaB6)
description: NIST Standard Reference Material SRM 660c, world-wide high-accuracy line profile calibrator.

name: Polypropylene (Isotactic)
description: Alpha-form isotactic PP, showing multiple sharp characteristic reflections due to its monoclinic packing.

name: Benzoic Acid
description: Monoclinic molecular crystal of benzoic acid, classic sublimation standard.

name: L-Alanine
description: Orthorhombic chiral amino acid crystal structure from CSD file reference.

name: Paracetamol (Form I)
description: Most stable monoclinic polymorph of acetaminophen, CSD reference standard.

name: PTFE (Teflon)
description: Highly helical crystalline polymer with a prominent reflection at 18.1° corresponding to interchain packing.

name: Nylon 6
description: Alpha crystalline monoclinic phase structured by hydrogen-bonded molecular chains.

name: Polyethylene Terephthalate
description: Semi-crystalline PET showing structural peaks induced via thermal holding or stretch orientation.

name: Aluminum
description: Face-centered cubic metal, ideal for standard cell calculation and educational indexing.

name: Gold Powder
description: Heavy chemical standard. Very high electron density creates brilliant reflections for instrument calibration.

name: Alpha Iron
description: Body-centered cubic Ferrite matrix, standard for structural steel alloying and phase analysis.

name: Cerium Oxide
description: Fluorite cubic oxide displaying high catalytic action; excellent for line profile grain size evaluations.

name: Titanium Dioxide (Anatase)
description: Metastable photoactive polymorph of titania, standard for thin-film solar cell validation and nanotechnology.

name: Sodium Chloride
description: Prototypical rock salt ionic structure, perfect for demonstrating structural factor absences.

name: Copper
description: Highly ordered metallic wire alloy substrate, showing characteristic intense peak shifts.

name: Silver
description: Brilliant conductive silver nanoparticles for studying size-strain properties through full-width indices.

name: Quartz (Alpha)
description: Trigonal quartz matrix. Extremely rich in low-symmetry peaks, frequently chosen for indexing exercises.

name: Beta-Quartz (High Quartz)
description: The high-temperature polymorph of quartz, stable above 573 °C (at ambient pressure).

name: Alpha-Cristobalite
description: Low-temperature, tetragonal polymorph of cristobalite.

name: Beta-Cristobalite
description: High-temperature cubic polymorph of cristobalite.

name: Alpha-Tridymite
description: Low-symmetry monoclinic polymorph of tridymite.

name: Beta-Tridymite
description: High-temperature hexagonal polymorph of tridymite.

name: Stishovite
description: Extremely dense, high-pressure rutile-structured silica.

name: Keatite
description: Synthetic tetragonal polymorph of silica.

name: Moganite
description: Monoclinic polymorph of silica.

name: Seifertite
description: Ultra-high-pressure polymorph of silica.

name: Coesite
description: A high-pressure monoclinic polymorph of silica.

name: Beryl (Be3Al2Si6O18)
description: Rare hexagonal ring silicate mineral structure from the RRUFF physical database.

name: Diamond
description: Sp³ carbon diamond-cubic framework with ultra-small unit cell sizes and sparse peaks.

name: Stem Cell Crystallin
description: Recombinant human stem cell crystallin protein featuring highly ordered beta-pleated sheets, serving as an advanced crystallographic profile for cellular scaffolds and organoid tracking.

name: Gamma-Crystallin (Eye Lens)
description: High-purity vertebrate eye lens gamma-crystallin protein specimen. Characterized by stable hydrophobic beta-barrel fold layers with excellent solution stability controls.

name: Alpha-A-Crystallin Subunit
description: Vertebrate core molecular heat shock alpha-A-crystallin protein complex structure, vital for maintaining cellular refraction stability.

name: Beta-B2-Crystallin Dimer
description: Major vertebrate lens structural beta-B2-crystallin protein. Shows stable dimeric assemblies preserving low-scattering characteristics.

name: Delta-Crystallin Lyase
description: Avian and reptile eye-lens specific delta-crystallin, structurally related to argininosuccinate lyase.

name: Collagen Triple-Helix
description: Fibrillar collagen microcrystalline matrix containing highly repeating glycine-proline-hydroxyproline triple helices.

name: Keratin-Alpha Filament
description: Fibrous alpha-helical structural keratin protein intermediate filament showing highly organized coiled-coil structures.

name: Silk Fibroin Beta-Sheet
description: Ordered beta-sheet structure of Bombyx mori silk protein, characterized by recurrent glycine-alanine-serine hexapeptides.

name: Human Insulin Hexamer
description: Recombinant human insulin hexameric crystal stabilized with zinc coordinates and phenolic ligands.

name: Bovine Serum Albumin
description: Polycrystalline bovine serum albumin transport protein specimen used as a reference point in biological small-angle scattering (SAXS).

name: Hen Egg White Lysozyme
description: Tetragonal hen egg-white lysozyme crystal. Used as the global benchmark protein crystal for calibrating biological XRD detectors.

name: Sperm Whale Myoglobin
description: Crystalline sperm whale myoglobin protein featuring the historic eight alpha-helix fold and a core active heme prosthetic coordination complex.

name: ECM Laminin Crystallin
description: Recombinant extracellular matrix (ECM) laminin-crystallin hybrid protein specimen. Organizes into a highly structured sheet-like hexagonal network suitable for cellular scaffolding and basement membrane modeling.

name: Crystalline DPPC Lipid
description: Crystallized dipalmitoylphosphatidylcholine (DPPC) lipid bilayer lattice. Demonstrates solid-gel phase sub-lattice alignment used to calibrate biomembrane structural dynamics scans.

name: Cholesteryl Palmitate Phase
description: Highly ordered organic crystal phase of cholesteryl palmitate ester. Crucial reference marker in modeling atherosclerotic calcified streaks and cell storage membrane boundaries.

name: Cholesterol Monohydrate
description: Crystalline form of cholesterol monohydrate. Found as a key plaque constituent in cardiovascular deposits and used as a calibration standard for biological lipid structures.

name: Crystalline Sphingomyelin
description: Highly ordered solid gel crystalline phase of milk-derived sphingomyelin. Essential for examining lipid-raft domain boundaries.

name: Palmitic Acid Crystal
description: Monoclinic B-form crystal structure of palmitic acid. Shows classic aliphatic chain packing with tilted dimer layers.

name: Stearic Acid Crystal B
description: Crystallized octadecanoic fatty acid (Stearic Acid) form B. Exhibits tight subcell packing used in thermal storage materials and pharmaceutical lubricant benchmarking.

name: Lauric Acid Crystal
description: Fully crystallized dodecanoic acid (Lauric Acid) structure. Features clean hydrogen-bonded carboxyl dimers providing extremely stable low-temperature melting curves.

name: DOPC Lipid Crystal
description: Low-temperature crystalline subphase of dioleoylphosphatidylcholine (DOPC). Key tool for researching liquid-crystalline ripple phases and trans-membrane peptide interactions.

name: POPE Lipid Crystal
description: Crystallized palmitoyloleoylphosphatidylethanolamine (POPE) phospholipid arrangement. Used for resolving structural curvatures and lipid-protein matching parameters.

name: Acetaminophen (Paracetamol Form I)
description: Crystalline Form I of acetaminophen (paracetamol). The thermodynamically stable monoclinic configuration at room temperature.

name: Ibuprofen Form I Standard
description: Crystalline phase of Ibuprofen (Form I). Demonstrates highly distinct, close-packed aliphatic molecular dimer geometries.

name: Carbamazepine Form III
description: Anticonvulsant active pharmaceutical ingredient crystalline phase; critical standard in drug polymorphism research.

name: Penicillin V Potassium
description: Crystalline phenomenomethylpenicillin potassium salt standard displaying rigid beta-lactam backbones with layered potassium channels.

name: Indomethacin Gamma-Form
description: Highly stable gamma-polymorph crystalline indomethacin standard. Commonly used to examine structural baselines of solid dispersions.

name: Naloxone Hydrochloride (Emergency Antagonist)
description: Emergency opioid receptor antagonist crystal. Highly ordered salt-hydrate form vital for molecular reversal of toxic levels of narcotics in first-responder medicine.

name: Codeine Phosphate Hemihydrate
description: Highly crystalline oral codeine salt reference phase, demonstrating dense networks of proton-sharing amine and phosphate groupings.

name: Atropine Sulfate Monohydrate
description: Cholinolytic muscarinic acetylcholine receptor blocker. Important clinical antidote standard used to counteract anticholesterase and organophosphate poisonings.

name: L-Ascorbic Acid (Vitamin C)
description: Vitamin C reference crystal featuring intensive intermolecular hydrogen-bonded systems that govern antioxidant electron transfer.

name: Diacetylmorphine HCl (Heroin)
description: Crystalline diacetylmorphine hydrochloride. A semi-synthetic opioid analgesic reference standard used extensively in forensic testing and illicit substance identification.

name: Ice-Binding Glycoprotein
description: Polar ice-binding glycoprotein template that forces surrounding water into a highly periodic, non-freezing liquid crystalline film to prevent cell lysis.

name: Crystalline Ice-Clathrate
description: Hexagonal Structure H clathrate hydrate consisting of a 34-water-molecule hosting network for bulkier bio-organic guest substances.

name: Deuterated Ice-Ih (Heavy Water)
description: Crystalline deuteurated heavy water ice Ih standard exhibiting minor anisotropic shift differences compared to light water ice.

name: Dry Ice Phase I (CO2)
description: Solid carbon dioxide Phase I (dry ice) crystallized at low temperatures. Linear CO2 symmetric crystal array.

name: Carbon Dioxide Clathrate Hydrate
description: Structure I carbon dioxide clathrate hydrate. Guest CO2 molecules trapped inside hydrogen-bonded water host cages.

name: Solid Alpha-Nitrogen (N2)
description: Low-temperature cubic solid nitrogen alpha phase stable below 35.6 K with ordered molecular orientations.

name: Solid Beta-Nitrogen (N2)
description: Hexagonal intermediate solid phase of molecular nitrogen preserving strong close-packed rotational disorder.

name: Cubic Poly-Nitrogen (cg-N)
description: Cubic gauche single-bonded polymeric nitrogen phase. Extrapolates to incredibly high covalent network density.

name: CO2-N2 Mixed Clathrate
description: Co-occupied mixed carbon dioxide and nitrogen hydrate crystal. Models gas storage dynamics under polar glaciers.

name: Crystalline Cyanuric Acid
description: Symmetric heterocyclic nitrogen-rich triazine standard. Planar hydrogen-bonded graphite-like network structure.

name: Crystalline Melamine
description: Highly structured amine derivative of s-triazine. Extensive hydrogen-bonding properties with wide industrial applications.

name: Crystalline Urea Reference
description: Highly pure organic crystalline urea reference. Classic template for guest-host channels and organic crystal engineering.

name: Beta-Carbon Nitride Phase
description: Hexagonal superhard beta-carbon nitride phase showcasing intense covalent C-N bonding network properties equivalent to diamond.

name: Barium Titanate
description: Classic ferroelectric perovskite demonstrating structural transitions between cubic and tetragonal.

name: Methylammonium Lead Iodide (MAPbI3) [ICSD]
description: Hybrid organic-inorganic perovskite solar cell material from the ICSD database.

name: Gallium Nitride
description: High-power wide-bandgap semiconductor configured extensively for modern solid-state green/blue lasers and power grids.

name: Molybdenum Disulfide
description: Monolayer transition metal dichalcogenide; prominent hexagonal structural shifts indicate solid-state shearing.

name: Titanium Carbide MXene (Ti3C2Tx)
description: A leading 2D transition metal carbide (MXene) nanomaterial showing highly characteristic basal plane (002) reflection at ultra-low angles due to expanded interlayer spacing. Highly prized for energy storage and electromagnetic shielding.

name: Graphene Oxide Nanosheets
description: Two-dimensional oxide-functionalized graphene sheet displaying a diagnostic interlayer (001) reflection at ultra-low angles. Ideal for graphene reduction studies.

name: Colloidal Gold Nanoparticles
description: Ultra-small face-centered cubic gold crystallites (12nm Average Size) exhibiting notable Scherrer peak broadening. Extensively used as reference models in size-broadening deconvolution.

name: Silver Nanowires (1D NWs)
description: Highly crystalline, high aspect ratio 1D silver nanowires showing strong preferred orientation along the (111) fiber normal. Essential for flexible transparent conductors.

name: Superparamagnetic Iron Oxide (SPIONs)
description: Nanosized magnetite spherical crystallites showcasing significant finite-size broadening corresponding to 8nm core grain diameters. Frequently monitored for bio-targeted magnetic resonance contrast agents and hyperthermia.

name: Titanium Dioxide Nanotubes (TiO2 NTs)
description: Anodized 1D anatase nanotube arrays with dominant (101) texturing. Benchmark photocatalyst database profile.

name: Cadmium Selenide Quantum Dots (CdSe QDs)
description: Pristine hexagonal wurtzite optoelectronic quantum dots showcasing highly symmetric grain core broadening. From standard ICSD databases.

name: Cesium Lead Bromide Nanocrystals (CsPbBr3)
description: Colloidal lead halide perovskite nanocubes showing supreme photoluminescent efficiency. Fingerprint orthorhombic database reference.

name: Quantum-Confined Silicon NPs
description: Quantum-confined silicon nanoparticles showing diagnostic amorphous core-shell scattering. Excellent validation profile from standard ICDD catalogs.

name: Exfoliated 2D MoS2 Nanosheets
description: High-surface-area exfoliated transition metal dichalcogenide nanosheets show significant dampening and shifting of basal plane peak intensities.

name: Zeolitic Imidazolate Framework-8 (ZIF-8)
description: Highly porous crystalline metal-organic framework (MOF) nanocrystals built for gas separation, showing signature low-angle nodes.

name: HKUST-1 MOF Nanocrystals
description: Highly ordered porous coordination framework featuring copper acetate wheels. Prevalent porous standard reference in the Cambridge Structural Database (CSD).

name: High-Purity Platinum (Pt)
description: Catalytically active precious face-centered cubic metal. Frequently used as a reliable high-pressure internal calibrant from COD database.

name: Tungsten Heavy Refractory (W)
description: Ultra-dense body-centered cubic tungsten element exhibiting immense high-temperature stabilization and minimal thermal expansion. Reference database index.

name: Nickel Nanospheres (Ni)
description: Pristine ferromagnetic face-centered cubic nickel nanocrystalline powder showing slight strain-induced asymmetry. COD reference.

name: High-Entropy Cantor Alloy
description: Equiatomic robust single-phase austenitic high-entropy alloy (HEA). Displays excellent cryogenic toughness and mechanical strength under high stress.

name: Refractory Tantalum Foil (Ta)
description: Corrosion resistant refractory cubic tantalum metal showing superb ductility and melting points above 3000°C.

name: Palladium Catalyst (Pd)
description: Prominent FCC heavy-metal catalyst nanocrystals optimized for organic synthesis, hydrogenation, and hydrogen filtration.

name: Refractory Niobium (Nb)
description: Premier body-centered cubic refractory metal. Widely used in superconducting cavities and high-temperature alloys.

name: Iridium Noble Metal (Ir)
description: The most corrosion-resistant metal known. FCC iridium is a standard reference for high-density metallic scattering.

name: Aluminum 6061-T6 Alloy
description: Precipitation-hardened structural aluminum alloy containing magnesium and silicon. Benchmark for aerospace structural characterization.

name: Nickel-Iron Permalloy (Ni80Fe20)
description: Extremely high magnetic permeability Nickel-Iron alloy (Permalloy). Crucial standard for soft magnetic thin-film research.

name: Copper Nanowires (1D Cu NWs)
description: Ultra-high aspect ratio 1D copper nanowires. Profiles exhibit strong (111) texturing and characteristic size/strain broadening from the ICDD nanomaterial database.

name: Silver Nanocubes (Plasmonic)
description: Shape-controlled silver nanocubes optimized for SERS and plasmonics. Shows distinct cubic symmetry and finite-size broadening fingerprints.

name: Tantalum Carbide (TaC)
description: Ultra-refractory interstitial carbide with extremely high melting point and metallic conductivity. Standard FCC-type interstitial reference.

name: Hardened Chromium Steel (S600)
description: M2 / S600 chromium-tungsten-molybdenum-vanadium high-speed tool steel (~4.2 wt% Cr, 6.4% W, 5.0% Mo, 1.9% V) in the quenched-and-tempered BCC/BCT martensitic state with dispersed M6C/MC carbides. Cubic Im-3m (No. 229) matrix, a = 2.872 Å.

name: Molybdenum Refractory (Mo)
description: High-temperature body-centered cubic refractory metal. Essential for calibrating thermal expansion and high-pressure XRD suites.

name: Pure Vanadium (V)
description: BCC transition metal with unique hydrogen absorption properties. Standard reference for group 5 metal characterization.

name: Rhodium Noble Metal (Rh)
description: Face-centered cubic platinum-group metal. Highly effective catalyst reference with distinctive high-angle diffraction signatures.

name: Lead Standard (Pb)
description: Soft FCC metallic standard. High atomic number (Z=82) results in intense X-ray scattering and significant absorption factors.

name: Bismuth Element (Bi)
description: Post-transition metal with rhombohedral symmetry. Large diamagnetism and low thermal conductivity baseline standard.

name: Beryllium Standard (Be)
description: Ultra-lightweight HCP elemental standard. High X-ray transparency makes it ideal for beam-window calibration.

name: Alpha Manganese (α-Mn)
description: Complex cubic α-phase manganese containing 58 atoms per unit cell. Exhibits a unique and extremely rich diffraction fingerprint.

name: Indium Standard (In)
description: Post-transition tetragonal soft metal. Low melting point makes it a premier standard for cryogenic and thermal XRD calibration.

name: Rhenium Refractory (Re)
description: Ultra-refractory HCP metal with one of the highest melting points. Critical for high-stress aerospace engine component characterization.

name: Osmium Element (Os)
description: The densest naturally occurring element. HCP noble metal standard exhibiting extreme hardness and oxidation resistance.

name: Wurtzite Gallium Nitride (GaN)
description: Hexagonal wurtzite Gallium Nitride. Essential wide bandgap semiconductor for power electronics, blue LEDs, and laser diodes.

name: Silicon Carbide (3C-SiC)
description: Beta structural polytype 3C-SiC. A crucial wide-bandgap compound semiconductor for high-temperature and high-power electronics.

name: Methylammonium Lead Iodide (MAPbI3) [COD]
description: The prototypical organic-inorganic hybrid halide perovskite. Revolutionized the field of low-cost solid-state solar cell absorbers.

name: Monolayer Molybdenum Disulfide (MoS2)
description: 2D layered transition metal dichalcogenide semiconductor with a direct bandgap when isolated to monolayer thickness.

name: NIST SRM 2910b (Synthetic Calcium Hydroxyapatite)
description: NIST Standard Reference Material 2910b is a highly refined synthetic Calcium Hydroxyapatite powder. It is certified for calcium-to-phosphorus stoichiometric ratios, phase purity, and crystal structure. Highly valued as the global benchmark standard for quantitative phase analysis of bones, biocomposites, osseointegrative dental coatings, and synthetic osteoregenerative grafts.

name: NIST SRM 1990 (Single-Crystal Silicon Orientation)
description: NIST SRM 1990 is a certified Single-Crystal Silicon orientation and lattice parameter standard. Specially designed for ultra-precise alignment of high-resolution X-ray goniometers, epitaxial thin film rocking-curves, wafer d-spacing calibration, and semiconductor texture profiling. Manufactured to extreme tolerances with negligible lattice defects.

name: NIST SRM 1878b (Respirable Crystalline Alpha-Quartz)
description: NIST Standard Reference Material 1878b is a high-purity crystalline alpha-quartz powder certified specifically for respirable crystalline silica (RCS) analysis. It serves as the primary calibration standard for occupational safety and hygiene laboratories worldwide to monitor, quantify, and mitigate toxic quartz dust levels in mining, construction, and stone-working environments.

name: Inconel 625 Nickel-Chromium Superalloy
description: A premium nickel-chromium-molybdenum solid-solution strengthened superalloy with nominal additions of niobium. Renowned for its exceptional high strength, outstanding fabrication properties, and superb corrosion resistance at elevated temperatures up to 982 °C. Heavily relied upon in aerospace turbine structures, exhaust systems, and critical chemical process equipment.

name: Kevlar-49 Aramid Fiber
description: High-performance Kevlar-49 aramid organic crystalline polymer fibers. Exhibits semi-crystalline diffraction features with characteristic (110) and (200) equatorial reflections. Prized as an aerospace reinforcement standard, displaying ultra-high tensile strength-to-weight ratio, high modulus, and outstanding ballistic protection properties.

name: Titanium Carbonitride MXene (Ti3CNTx)
description: An advanced titanium carbonitride MXene 2D material. Formed by selective chemical etching of Al layers from Ti3AlCN MAX phase precursors. Features exceptional metallic conductivity, high electromagnetic interference shielding efficiency (EMI shielding), and exceptional electrochemical performance for ultra-fast supercapacitor electrodes.

name: 45S5 Bioglass-Ceramic (Hench Glass)
description: Original bioactive Hench glass-ceramic (45SiO2-24.5CaO-24.5Na2O-6P2O5). Upon physiological immersion in simulated body fluid (SBF), it rapidly forms an osteoconductive hydroxycarbonate apatite (HCA) surface layer that bonds strongly with soft and hard tissue.

name: Dicalcium Phosphate Dihydrate (DCPD / Brushite)
description: Fast-setting, acidic calcium phosphate mineral ubiquitous in self-setting resorbable orthopedic bone cements. Dissolves under physiological conditions to promote active endogenous bone remodeling.

name: Monocalcium Phosphate Monohydrate (MCPM)
description: Highly soluble acidic calcium phosphate component used in dual-component surgical bone cements. Reacts rapidly with basic calcium salts (such as TTCP or CaO) to yield resorbable brushite or hydroxyapatite matrices.

name: Tetracalcium Phosphate (TTCP / Hilgenstockite)
description: The most basic calcium phosphate phase (Ca/P molar ratio = 2.0). Serves as the key reactant in apatitic self-setting calcium phosphate cements, reacting with acidic phosphates to form hydroxyapatite at body temperature without exothermicity.

name: Strontium-Substituted Hydroxyapatite (Sr-HAp 10 mol%)
description: Bioactive osteoinductive bioceramic incorporating 10 mol% strontium ions. Strontium replacement for calcium stimulates osteoblast cell proliferation while inhibiting osteoclast activity, offering targeted treatment for osteoporotic bone defects.

name: Fluorapatite (FAp)
description: Fluorinated calcium phosphate bioceramic (Ca10(PO4)6F2). Fluoride ion substitution into the apatite channel dramatically increases thermal stability and lowers chemical solubility in acidic oral environments, conferring superior dental caries resistance.

name: Mineral Trioxide Aggregate (MTA)
description: Surgical endodontic biocompatible cement mixture composed primarily of tricalcium silicate, dicalcium silicate, tricalcium aluminate, and radiopaque bismuth oxide (Bi2O3). Sets in moist physiological tissue to form calcium silicate hydrate gel and bio-interactive calcium hydroxide.

name: Y-TZP Zirconia Dental Bioceramic (3Y-TZP)
description: Yttria-stabilized tetragonal zirconia polycrystal ceramic (3 mol% Y2O3). Renowned for stress-induced phase transformation toughening (t -> m transition at crack tips), providing unprecedented fracture toughness (>8 MPa·m1/2) for structural all-ceramic dental crowns and orthopedic joint implants.

name: Bioactive Glass 13-93 Scaffold
description: FDA-cleared resorbable bioactive silicate glass (53SiO2-6Na2O-12K2O-5MgO-20CaO-4P2O5) specifically engineered for 3D printed porous bone tissue engineering scaffolds. Viscous flow sintering processing enables intricate trabecular architecture creation.

name: Paracetamol (Acetaminophen) Form I (Monoclinic)
description: Thermodynamically stable monoclinic crystalline polymorph Form I of paracetamol (4-acetamidophenol) active pharmaceutical ingredient (API). Characterized by hydrogen-bonded corrugated sheet sub-layers; benchmark standard for solid-state drug formulation quality control.

name: Paracetamol (Acetaminophen) Form II (Orthorhombic)
description: Metastable orthorhombic polymorph Form II of paracetamol. Features parallel hydrogen-bonded planar layers that undergo slip deformation under compression, imparting exceptional direct compressibility without requiring wet granulation binders.

name: Aspirin (Acetylsalicylic Acid) Form I
description: Monoclinic crystal Form I of acetylsalicylic acid analgesic active pharmaceutical ingredient. Features centro-symmetric carboxylic acid dimers linked by intermolecular hydrogen bonding in a monoclinic lattice.

name: Metformin Hydrochloride Form I
description: Thermodynamically stable monoclinic crystal Form I of biguanide antidiabetic API metformin HCl. Exhibits dense ionic salt hydrogen bonding networks between protonated biguanidinium cations and chloride anions.

name: Alpha-Lactose Monohydrate (Pharma Excipient)
description: Crystalline disaccharide monohydrate excipient ubiquitous in solid dosage tablet compression. Serves as a primary diluent, binder, and carrier crystal in dry powder inhaler (DPI) formulations owing to consistent surface energy and compaction behavior.

name: Microcrystalline Cellulose (MCC I-beta)
description: Purified, partially depolymerized alpha-cellulose crystalline excipient (Native Cellulose I-beta). Recognized as the supreme direct-compression tableting binder due to exceptional plastic deformation and mechanical interlocking under compaction pressure.

name: Beta-D-Mannitol (Pharma Grade Excipient)
description: Crystalline sugar alcohol beta-polymorph excipient prized in orally disintegrating tablets (ODTs) and freeze-dried lyophilized protein biopharmaceuticals. Offers non-hygroscopic protection and a cooling, pleasant mouthfeel.

name: Polyvinylidene Fluoride (α-PVDF, Form II)
description: Non-polar, thermodynamically stable melt-crystallized polymorph of polyvinylidene fluoride adopting antiparallel TGTG' helical chain packing. Monoclinic P21/c (No. 14), a = 4.96 Å, b = 9.64 Å, c = 4.62 Å, β = 90.0°, Z = 4, PDF 00-042-1650.

name: Polyvinylidene Fluoride (β-PVDF, Form I — Piezoelectric)
description: Ferroelectric and piezoelectric polar polymorph of PVDF with all-trans (TTTT) planar zigzag chains aligned in parallel dipoles, produced by uniaxial stretching or electrospinning. Orthorhombic Cm2m (No. 38), a = 8.58 Å, b = 4.91 Å, c = 2.56 Å, Z = 2, PDF 00-038-1638.

name: Polyvinylidene Fluoride (γ-PVDF, Form III)
description: Intermediate polar polymorph of PVDF crystallizing from polar solvents (DMSO/DMAc) or high-temperature annealing (~160 °C) in a TTTGTTTG' chain conformation. Monoclinic Cc (No. 9), a = 4.96 Å, b = 9.58 Å, c = 9.23 Å, β = 92.9°, Z = 8.

name: Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE Form IV, 15/7 Helix)
description: Ambient room-temperature crystalline polymorph of polytetrafluoroethylene (stable 19–30 °C) composed of tightly packed 15/7 fluorocarbon helices. Trigonal P31 (No. 144), a = 5.66 Å, c = 19.50 Å, PDF 00-047-2217. Displays an iconic ultra-sharp (100) peak at 18.08° 2θ.

name: Polyoxymethylene (POM, Trigonal Acetal Homopolymer)
description: Highly crystalline (70–85%) engineering acetal thermoplastic consisting of helical 9/5 (CH2O)n chains packed in a trigonal lattice. Trigonal P31 (No. 144), a = 4.470 Å, c = 17.390 Å, PDF 00-049-2120. Renowned for high stiffness, dimensional stability, and low friction.

name: Polyethylene Oxide (PEO, Crystalline Monoclinic)
description: Semi-crystalline polyether adopting a 7/2 helical conformation in a monoclinic lattice. Monoclinic P21/a (No. 14), a = 8.05 Å, b = 13.04 Å, c = 19.48 Å, β = 125.4°, PDF 00-049-2201. Benchmark host matrix for solid polymer lithium electrolytes (PEO-LiTFSI).

name: Polyvinyl Alcohol (PVA, Crystalline Monoclinic)
description: Water-soluble semi-crystalline polymer stabilized by dense intermolecular O–H···O hydrogen-bonded sheets of planar zigzag chains. Monoclinic P21/m (No. 11), a = 7.81 Å, b = 2.52 Å, c = 5.51 Å, β = 91.7°, Z = 2.

name: Nylon 6,6 (Polyamide 66, α-Form)
description: Triclinic α-polymorph of poly(hexamethylene adipamide) featuring fully extended planar zigzag chains linked into hydrogen-bonded sheets that progressively shift along the chain axis. Triclinic P-1 (No. 2), a = 4.90 Å, b = 5.40 Å, c = 17.20 Å, α = 48.5°, β = 77.0°, γ = 63.5°, Z = 1, PDF 00-043-1662.

name: Nylon 12 (Polyamide 12, γ-Form)
description: Pseudo-hexagonal monoclinic γ-polymorph of polylaurolactam (PA12), the standard crystalline phase in selective laser sintering (SLS) 3D printing powders. Monoclinic P21/c (No. 14), a = 4.79 Å, b = 31.90 Å, c = 9.58 Å, β = 120.0°, Z = 4.

name: Polybutylene Terephthalate (PBT, α-Form)
description: Relaxed triclinic α-polymorph of fast-crystallizing aromatic polyester PBT with gauche-trans-gauche tetramethylene segments (reversibly transforms to β-PBT under tensile stress). Triclinic P-1 (No. 2), a = 4.83 Å, b = 5.94 Å, c = 11.59 Å, α = 99.7°, β = 115.2°, γ = 110.8°, Z = 1.

name: Polyethylene Naphthalate (PEN, α-Form)
description: High-Tg semi-crystalline naphthalene-ring polyester offering superior O2/CO2 barrier and thermal stability over PET. Triclinic P-1 (No. 2), a = 6.51 Å, b = 5.75 Å, c = 13.20 Å, α = 81.3°, β = 144.0°, γ = 100.0°, Z = 1.

name: Polyphenylene Sulfide (PPS)
description: High-performance flame-retardant semi-crystalline engineering thermoplastic with alternating phenylene rings tilted ±45° relative to the sulfide zigzag plane. Orthorhombic Pbcn (No. 60), a = 8.67 Å, b = 5.61 Å, c = 10.26 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-049-2214.

name: Isotactic Polypropylene (β-iPP, Trigonal Polymorph)
description: Frustrated trigonal β-modification of isotactic polypropylene (3 isochiral 3/1 helices per cell) induced by β-nucleating agents or shear flow; imparts dramatically higher impact toughness than monoclinic α-iPP. Trigonal P3121 (No. 152), a = 11.01 Å, c = 6.50 Å, Z = 9, with diagnostic strong 16.09° (110) peak.

name: Syndiotactic Polystyrene (sPS, α-Form)
description: High-melting (Tm ≈ 270 °C) crystalline engineering polystyrene formed via metallocene catalysis with all-trans planar zigzag triplets arranged in a trigonal lattice. Trigonal P-3c1 (No. 165), a = 26.26 Å, c = 5.04 Å, Z = 18.

name: Poly(1-butene) (PB-1, Form I — Trigonal)
description: Thermodynamically stable twinned trigonal polymorph of isotactic poly(1-butene) (3/1 helical chains) that forms spontaneously via solid-state transformation from tetragonal Form II upon aging at room temperature. Trigonal R-3c (No. 167), a = 17.70 Å, c = 6.50 Å, Z = 18.

name: Poly(3-hexylthiophene) (P3HT, Regioregular Semiconducting Polymer)
description: Benchmark π-conjugated crystalline semiconducting polymer self-assembling into edge-on or face-on lamellae with sharp (h00) alkyl side-chain lamellar orders (d100 = 16.40 Å) and (020) π–π stacking reflection at 23.39° (d = 3.80 Å). Monoclinic P21/c (No. 14), a = 16.40 Å, b = 7.60 Å, c = 7.80 Å, β = 90.0°.

name: Polyacrylonitrile (PAN, Hexagonal Mesocrystalline)
description: Rod-like dipole-coupled polymer chains packed in a laterally ordered hexagonal lattice; the dominant precursor for aerospace-grade carbon fibers upon thermal stabilization and carbonization. Hexagonal P6/mmm (No. 191), a = 6.00 Å, c = 5.10 Å, characterized by its sharp 17.05° (100) equatorial peak.

name: Poly(butylene succinate) (PBS, α-Form Biodegradable Polyester)
description: Bio-based biodegradable aliphatic polyester crystallizing in the monoclinic α-form with T7GTG' chain conformation (transforms to β-PBS under tensile strain). Monoclinic P21/n (No. 14), a = 5.23 Å, b = 9.12 Å, c = 10.90 Å, β = 123.9°, Z = 2.

name: Manganese Ferrite (MnFe2O4, Magnetic Hyperthermia)
description: High-magnetization soft spinel ferrite (Ms ≈ 80–90 emu/g) widely used for magnetic fluid hyperthermia (MFH) and dual-mode T2 MRI theranostics due to superior Néel relaxation Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) and low cytotoxicity. Cubic Fd-3m (No. 227), a = 8.499 Å, Z = 8, PDF 00-010-0319.

name: Magnesium Ferrite (MgFe2O4, Biocompatible Hyperthermia)
description: Heavy-metal-free biocompatible partially inverse spinel ferrite engineered for clinical magnetic hyperthermia without Co/Ni ion leaching risk. Cubic Fd-3m (No. 227), a = 8.389 Å, Z = 8, PDF 00-036-0398.

name: Manganese-Zinc Ferrite (Mn0.5Zn0.5Fe2O4, Tunable-Tc Hyperthermia)
description: Mixed spinel ferrite where non-magnetic Zn2+ substitution on tetrahedral A-sites maximizes saturation magnetization and tunes the Curie temperature (Tc) downward toward self-regulating therapeutic hyperthermia windows. Cubic Fd-3m (No. 227), a = 8.462 Å, Z = 8.

name: Zinc-Cobalt Ferrite (Zn0.4Co0.6Fe2O4, High-Anisotropy Hyperthermia)
description: Anisotropy-engineered Zn-doped cobalt ferrite nanoparticle phase balancing high Co2+ magnetocrystalline anisotropy with Zn2+ magnetization enhancement to deliver ultra-high Specific Loss Power (>1000 W/g) at low clinical AMF amplitudes. Cubic Fd-3m (No. 227), a = 8.405 Å, Z = 8.

name: Nickel-Zinc Ferrite (Ni0.5Zn0.5Fe2O4, Magnetic Hyperthermia)
description: Soft cubic spinel ferrite with high electrical resistivity and tunable hysteresis/relaxation heating under 100–500 kHz alternating magnetic fields. Cubic Fd-3m (No. 227), a = 8.382 Å, Z = 8, PDF 00-008-0234.

name: Copper-Zinc Ferrite (Cu0.5Zn0.5Fe2O4, Self-Regulating Hyperthermia)
description: Cubic spinel ferrite combining Zn-lowered Curie temperature for controlled magnetic hyperthermia with intrinsic Cu2+ antibacterial activity for post-surgical oncology implants. Cubic Fd-3m (No. 227), a = 8.395 Å, Z = 8.

name: Lanthanum Strontium Manganite (La0.75Sr0.25MnO3, Self-Regulating Hyperthermia)
description: Landmark self-regulating Curie-temperature (Tc ≈ 42–46 °C via Sr/Ti/Ag stoichiometry tuning) perovskite manganite (LSMO) that automatically transitions from ferromagnetic to paramagnetic above therapeutic tumor-ablation temperatures, preventing overheating of healthy tissue. Trigonal R-3c (No. 167), a = 5.512 Å, c = 13.368 Å, Z = 6, PDF 00-051-0409.

name: Lanthanum Calcium Manganite (La0.8Ca0.2MnO3, Curie-Limited Hyperthermia)
description: Orthorhombic perovskite manganite (LCMO) exhibiting a sharp ferromagnetic-to-paramagnetic phase transition tunable into the 41–45 °C therapeutic window for self-controlled magnetic hyperthermia without invasive thermometry. Orthorhombic Pnma (No. 62), a = 5.475 Å, b = 7.738 Å, c = 5.485 Å, Z = 4.

name: Cu-Ni Ferromagnetic Thermoseed (Cu30Ni70, Self-Regulating Hyperthermia)
description: Clinically validated FCC solid-solution copper-nickel alloy engineered to possess a Curie temperature near 45–50 °C for interstitial self-regulating thermoseed hyperthermia of deep solid tumors (prostate, glioblastoma, hepatic lesions). Cubic Fm-3m (No. 225), a = 3.551 Å, Z = 4.

name: L10 Iron-Platinum Alloy (L10-FePt, High-SAR Hyperthermia)
description: Chemically ordered face-centered-tetragonal (L10) FePt intermetallic nanocrystals featuring diagnostic (001) and (110) superlattice ordering reflections, giant magnetocrystalline anisotropy for high-SAR hyperthermia, and strong Pt X-ray CT/MRI dual-modal contrast. Tetragonal P4/mmm (No. 123), a = 3.852 Å, c = 3.713 Å, Z = 2, PDF 00-043-1359.

name: Magnetite-Hydroxyapatite Composite (Fe3O4-HAp, Bone Hyperthermia)
description: Biphasic osteoconductive magnetic bioceramic combining Cubic Fe3O4 (Fd-3m) magnetic heating domains with Hexagonal Hydroxyapatite (P63/m) bone-mineral matrix for simultaneous osteosarcoma hyperthermia ablation and post-resection bone regeneration.

name: Ferrimagnetic Bioactive Glass-Ceramic (CaSiO3-Fe3O4, Bone Hyperthermia)
description: Kokubo-type bioactive ferrimagnetic glass-ceramic crystallizing Monoclinic β-wollastonite (CaSiO3, P21/c) and Cubic magnetite (Fe3O4, Fd-3m) inside a CaO-SiO2-Fe2O3 matrix; bonds chemically to living bone via surface apatite formation while generating 43–46 °C localized AMF hyperthermia.

name: Magnesium Ferrite-Beta-TCP Scaffold (MgFe2O4-β-TCP, Bioresorbable Hyperthermia)
description: Bioresorbable magnetic bone-graft composite combining biocompatible Cubic MgFe2O4 (Fd-3m) hyperthermia grains with Trigonal β-tricalcium phosphate (R3c) for gradual resorption and new bone ingrowth following hyperthermic tumor eradication.

name: Covellite Copper Sulfide (CuS, NIR Photothermal Hyperthermia)
description: Semiconducting covellite CuS nanocrystals exhibiting intense d–d transition and localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) absorption in the NIR-I/NIR-II biological windows (808–1064 nm) for high-efficiency photothermal hyperthermia (PTT) and photoacoustic tumor imaging. Hexagonal P63/mmc (No. 194), a = 3.792 Å, c = 16.344 Å, Z = 6, PDF 00-006-0464.

name: Oxygen-Deficient Tungsten Oxide (W18O49, NIR Photothermal Hyperthermia)
description: Sub-stoichiometric Magnéli-phase monoclinic tungsten oxide (WO2.72) nanowires rich in oxygen vacancies and W5+/W6+ polaron states, delivering strong NIR photothermal hyperthermia (>45% conversion efficiency), radiosensitization, and high-Z X-ray CT contrast. Monoclinic P2/m (No. 10), a = 18.334 Å, b = 3.786 Å, c = 14.044 Å, β = 115.20°, PDF 00-005-0392.

name: Gold Nanorods / Nanoshells (Au, Plasmonic Photothermal Hyperthermia)
description: Biocompatible FCC crystalline gold nanostructures (AuroLase-class nanoshells and aspect-ratio-tuned nanorods) exhibiting tunable NIR longitudinal surface plasmon resonance (780–1064 nm) for focal photothermal hyperthermia ablation of solid tumors. Cubic Fm-3m (No. 225), a = 4.0782 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-004-0784.

name: Alpha-Prime Titanium Martensite (α'-Ti, Acicular HCP)
description: Supersaturated hexagonal acicular martensite (α'-Ti) formed during rapid cooling from the β phase field (e.g., water-quenched or as-built Laser Powder Bed Fusion LPBF Ti-6Al-4V). Contracted lattice shifts peaks to higher 2θ vs equilibrium α-Ti. Hexagonal P63/mmc (No. 194), a = 2.922 Å, c = 4.664 Å, Z = 2.

name: Alpha-Double-Prime Titanium Martensite (α''-Ti, Orthorhombic)
description: Soft orthorhombic thermoelastic / stress-induced martensite (α''-Ti) forming in β-stabilized Ti-Nb, Ti-Mo, and Ti-V shape-memory and superelastic biomedical alloys. Diagnostic doublet splitting of (110)/(020) and (111)/(021) reflections distinguishes α'' from HCP α'. Orthorhombic Cmcm (No. 63), a = 3.010 Å, b = 4.950 Å, c = 4.680 Å, Z = 4.

name: Ti-5Al-2.5Sn (Grade 6, Cryogenic α-Titanium Alloy)
description: Single-phase solid-solution-strengthened α-titanium alloy (Grade 6 / ELI) offering exceptional weldability, creep strength, and fracture toughness down to liquid-helium temperatures (4 K) without ductile-to-brittle transition. Hexagonal P63/mmc (No. 194), a = 2.931 Å, c = 4.692 Å.

name: Ti-3Al-2.5V (Grade 9, Aerospace Hydraulic Tubing Alloy)
description: Near-α / lean α+β titanium alloy ('Half 6-4', ASTM Grade 9) combining 50% higher strength than CP-Ti with superior cold-formability for seamless aerospace hydraulic lines and honeycomb cores. Hexagonal α (P63/mmc) matrix with minor BCC β (Im-3m).

name: Ti-6Al-2Sn-4Zr-2Mo (Ti-6242, High-Temp Jet Engine Alloy)
description: Silicon-modified near-α high-temperature titanium alloy (Ti-6242S) engineered for superior creep resistance and oxidation stability up to 540 °C in gas-turbine compressor disks and blades. Hexagonal α (P63/mmc) + retained Cubic β (Im-3m).

name: Ti-6Al-2Sn-4Zr-6Mo (Ti-6246, Deep-Hardenable α+β Alloy)
description: β-rich α+β aerospace forging alloy offering higher room- and intermediate-temperature strength and deeper section hardenability than Ti-6242 via elevated 6 wt.% Mo β-stabilization. Hexagonal α (P63/mmc) + Cubic β (Im-3m).

name: Ti-6Al-6V-2Sn (Ti-662, High-Strength Aerospace α+β Alloy)
description: High-strength heat-treatable α+β titanium alloy strengthened by higher vanadium, tin, copper, and iron additions (UTS > 1150 MPa in STA condition). Hexagonal α (P63/mmc) + Cubic β (Im-3m).

name: Ti-6Al-7Nb (Biomedical V-Free α+β Implant Alloy, ISO 5832-11)
description: Clinically certified vanadium-free biomedical α+β titanium alloy (ISO 5832-11 / ASTM F1295) replacing cytotoxic V in Ti-6Al-4V with biocompatible Nb while retaining high fatigue strength and passive TiO2/Nb2O5 corrosion resistance. Hexagonal α (P63/mmc) + Cubic β (Im-3m).

name: Ti-5Al-5Mo-5V-3Cr (Ti-5553, Aerospace Near-β Forging Alloy)
description: Ultra-high-strength, deep-hardenable near-β aerospace forging alloy (UTS up to 1300 MPa) with a BCC β matrix reinforced by fine precipitated α laths; standard material for widebody commercial aircraft landing-gear beams. Cubic β (Im-3m) + Hexagonal α (P63/mmc).

name: Ti-13Nb-13Zr (Biomedical Low-Modulus Near-β Alloy, ASTM F1713)
description: Al- and V-free biocompatible near-β orthopedic titanium alloy (ASTM F1713) exhibiting low elastic modulus (~79 GPa) to minimize bone stress shielding and superior wear/corrosion resistance via ZrO2-enriched passive film. Cubic β (Im-3m) + Hexagonal α'/α (P63/mmc).

name: Ti-15Mo (Biomedical β-Titanium Alloy, ASTM F2066)
description: Single-phase solution-treated metastable BCC β-titanium biomedical alloy (ASTM F2066) offering low elastic modulus (78 GPa), MRI-compatible low magnetic susceptibility, and exceptional resistance to crevice corrosion in body fluids. Cubic Im-3m (No. 229), a = 3.268 Å, Z = 2.

name: Ti-35Nb-7Zr-5Ta (TNZT, Ultra-Low-Modulus Biomedical β-Alloy)
description: Second-generation ultra-low-modulus (~55 GPa, closest among load-bearing metals to cortical bone 15–30 GPa) single-phase BCC β-titanium alloy composed exclusively of non-toxic valve metals (Ti, Nb, Zr, Ta). Cubic Im-3m (No. 229), a = 3.298 Å, Z = 2.

name: Ti-29Nb-13Ta-4.6Zr (TNTZ, Gum-Metal Biomedical β-Alloy)
description: Niinomi-type single-phase BCC β-titanium biomedical alloy with near-bone elastic modulus (~58 GPa), high elastic admissible strain, and complete freedom from Al/V/Ni ions. Cubic Im-3m (No. 229), a = 3.292 Å, Z = 2.

name: Ti-12Mo-6Zr-2Fe (TMZF, Orthopedic β-Alloy, ASTM F1813)
description: Clinically deployed single-phase BCC β-titanium orthopedic alloy (ASTM F1813) offering high notch-fatigue strength, 25% lower modulus (~74 GPa) than Ti-6Al-4V, and superior corrosion-fatigue resistance in total hip prostheses. Cubic Im-3m (No. 229), a = 3.274 Å, Z = 2.

name: Beta-C Titanium (Ti-3Al-8V-6Cr-4Mo-4Zr, Grade 19)
description: Deep-hardenable metastable BCC β-titanium alloy (ASTM Grade 19 / Ti-38644) combining cold formability in the solution-treated β state with age-hardenable tensile strengths exceeding 1350 MPa and immunity to hot-chloride stress corrosion cracking. Cubic Im-3m (No. 229), a = 3.242 Å, Z = 2.

name: Gamma Titanium Aluminide (γ-TiAl, L10 Intermetallic)
description: Ordered face-centered-tetragonal L10 intermetallic (TiAl; Ti-48Al-2Cr-2Nb class) delivering half the density of Ni-base superalloys with oxidation and creep resistance up to 750–850 °C; features diagnostic (001)/(110) superlattice reflections and (002)/(200) tetragonality splitting. Tetragonal P4/mmm (No. 123), a = 4.005 Å, c = 4.070 Å, c/a = 1.016, Z = 2, PDF 00-005-0678.

name: Alpha-2 Titanium Aluminide (α2-Ti3Al, D019 Intermetallic)
description: Ordered hexagonal D019 superstructure intermetallic (a ≈ 2a_α) coexisting with γ-TiAl in fully lamellar TiAl turbine-blade alloys; identified by characteristic (101) and (110) superlattice reflections at 26.14° and 30.91° 2θ. Hexagonal P63/mmc (No. 194), a = 5.782 Å, c = 4.647 Å, Z = 2, PDF 00-014-0451.

name: Orthorhombic O-Phase Titanium Aluminide (Ti2AlNb)
description: Ordered orthorhombic O-phase titanium aluminide (Ti2AlNb) offering superior room-temperature ductility, fracture toughness, and 650–700 °C creep strength over α2-Ti3Al alloys. Orthorhombic Cmcm (No. 63), a = 6.089 Å, b = 9.569 Å, c = 4.667 Å, Z = 4.

name: Nitinol Austenite (B2-NiTi, Superelastic Cubic Phase)
description: Ordered CsCl-type (B2) cubic parent austenite phase of equiatomic nickel-titanium (Nitinol), stable at body temperature in superelastic cardiovascular stents and orthodontic archwires; undergoes reversible stress-induced B2 ↔ B19' martensitic transformation. Cubic Pm-3m (No. 221), a = 3.015 Å, Z = 1, PDF 00-018-0899.

name: Epsilon-Cobalt (ε-Co, β-Mn Cubic Metastable Phase)
description: Metastable primitive cubic (β-Mn-type) allotrope of pure cobalt synthesized via solution chemistry or rapid condensation, containing 20 atoms per unit cell across two inequivalent crystallographic sites; transforms to HCP/FCC cobalt upon annealing above 300 °C. Cubic P4132 (No. 213), a = 6.097 Å, Z = 20, PDF 01-089-7373.

name: Delta-Chromium (δ-Cr, A15 Cubic Thin-Film Phase)
description: Metastable A15 (Cr3Si-type) topologically close-packed cubic polymorph of pure chromium formed in sputtered PVD thin films and gas-evaporated nanoparticles; characterized by its diagnostic (200)/(210)/(211) triplet and irreversible transformation to BCC α-Cr above 450 °C. Cubic Pm-3n (No. 223), a = 4.588 Å, Z = 8, PDF 00-019-0323.

name: Co-28Cr-6Mo Wrought Alloy (ASTM F1537 / ISO 5832-12)
description: Thermomechanically forged and annealed low-carbon biomedical cobalt-chromium-molybdenum alloy (Co-28Cr-6Mo, <0.14 wt% C) stabilized predominantly in the fine-grained metastable γ-FCC solid-solution phase for extreme fatigue and wear resistance in orthopedic hip/knee implants. Cubic Fm-3m (No. 225), a = 3.574 Å, Z = 4.

name: Co-28Cr-6Mo HCP Martensitic Phase (ε-CoCrMo)
description: Hexagonal close-packed ε-martensite phase formed in Co-28Cr-6Mo biomedical implants via isothermal aging (750–850 °C) or severe plastic deformation (SIMT) on articulating joint bearing surfaces; distinguished from γ-FCC CoCrMo by its prominent (100) at 41.20° and (101) at 47.02° reflections. Hexagonal P63/mmc (No. 194), a = 2.528 Å, c = 4.098 Å, Z = 2.

name: MP35N Multiphase Superalloy (Co-35Ni-20Cr-10Mo, ASTM F562)
description: Work-hardenable, non-magnetic cobalt-nickel-chromium-molybdenum multiphase superalloy (35Co-35Ni-20Cr-10Mo) combining ultra-high tensile strength (>1800 MPa), sulfide stress-cracking immunity, and biocompatibility for cardiac pacing leads and aerospace fasteners. Cubic Fm-3m (No. 225), a = 3.592 Å, Z = 4.

name: Vitallium Dental & Orthopedic Alloy (Co-30Cr-5Mo-C)
description: Classic cast cobalt-chromium-molybdenum prosthetic alloy (Co-30Cr-5Mo-0.4C) exhibiting a dual-phase γ-FCC (Fm-3m, a = 3.578 Å) and ε-HCP (P63/mmc, a = 2.530 Å, c = 4.104 Å) dendritic solid solution reinforced by interdendritic M23C6 carbides.

name: Co-28Cr-9W Dental Alloy (SLM / CAD-CAM CoCrW, ISO 22674)
description: Nickel- and beryllium-free cobalt-chromium-tungsten dental alloy tailored for selective laser melting (SLM) and CAD/CAM milling of porcelain-fused-to-metal (PFM) crowns and bridges; dual-phase γ-FCC (a = 3.584 Å) + ε-HCP (a = 2.534 Å, c = 4.112 Å) matrix.

name: Stellite 12 Cobalt Hardfacing Alloy (Co-30Cr-8.5W-1.4C)
description: High-carbon cobalt-chromium-tungsten hardfacing alloy (30% Cr, 8.5% W, 1.4% C) with higher carbide volume fraction (Cr7C3/M23C6) and greater hot abrasion resistance than Stellite 6, embedded in a dual-phase FCC/HCP Co-Cr matrix (a_fcc = 3.582 Å).

name: Stellite 21 High-Temp Corrosion Alloy (Co-27Cr-5.5Mo-2.8Ni)
description: Low-carbon cobalt-chromium-molybdenum-nickel hardfacing superalloy (27% Cr, 5.5% Mo, 2.8% Ni, 0.25% C) engineered for thermal-shock, galling, cavitation-erosion, and hot-acid corrosion resistance; single-phase γ-FCC solid solution stabilized by Ni. Cubic Fm-3m (No. 225), a = 3.576 Å, Z = 4.

name: Haynes 188 Cobalt Superalloy (Co-22Cr-22Ni-14W-La)
description: Solid-solution-strengthened cobalt-nickel-chromium-tungsten sheet superalloy (Co-22Cr-22Ni-14W-0.03La) offering exceptional oxidation resistance up to 1095 °C via adherent lanthanum-modified Cr2O3 scales and high creep-rupture strength. Cubic Fm-3m (No. 225), a = 3.588 Å, Z = 4.

name: MAR-M 509 Cast Cobalt Superalloy (Co-23.5Cr-10Ni-7W-3.5Ta)
description: Investment-cast cobalt-base turbine superalloy (Co-23.5Cr-10Ni-7W-3.5Ta-0.6C) strengthened by solid-solution W/Ta and script-like TaC/M23C6 carbides within a high-melting γ-FCC Co-Cr-Ni matrix for hot-gas-path stator vanes. Cubic Fm-3m (No. 225), a = 3.586 Å, Z = 4.

name: Co-9Al-9W γ'-Strengthened Cobalt Superalloy (L12 Co3(Al,W))
description: Next-generation γ/γ' precipitation-hardened cobalt-aluminum-tungsten superalloy containing coherent cuboidal L12-ordered Co3(Al,W) precipitates (Cu3Au-type) exhibiting anomalous yield-strength increase at elevated temperatures and diagnostic (100)/(110) superlattice reflections. Cubic Pm-3m (No. 221), a = 3.599 Å, Z = 1.

name: Ultimet Wear & Corrosion Alloy (Co-26Cr-9Ni-5Mo-3Fe-2W)
description: Wrought and weld-overlay cobalt-chromium-nickel-molybdenum alloy (UNS R31233) bridging Hastelloy-grade wet acid corrosion resistance with Stellite-grade cavitation erosion and galling resistance via strain-induced work hardening. Cubic Fm-3m (No. 225), a = 3.579 Å, Z = 4.

name: Permendur 49 Soft Magnetic Alloy (Fe-49Co-2V, Ordered B2)
description: Equiatomic iron-cobalt-vanadium soft magnetic alloy (Hiperco 50 / Permendur 49) exhibiting the highest saturation magnetic flux density (~2.4 T) of any commercial alloy, crystallizing in the CsCl-type ordered B2 cubic structure with weak (100)/(111) superlattice peaks. Cubic Pm-3m (No. 221), a = 2.857 Å, Z = 1, PDF 00-049-1567.

name: Samarium-Cobalt 1:5 Permanent Magnet (SmCo5)
description: Rare-earth cobalt permanent magnet intermetallic (CaCu5-type structure) possessing enormous uniaxial magnetocrystalline anisotropy (Ha > 25 T), extreme coercivity, and high Curie temperature (720 °C) for high-temperature motors and microwave tubes. Hexagonal P6/mmm (No. 191), a = 5.002 Å, c = 3.970 Å, Z = 1, PDF 00-027-1122.

name: Alnico 5 Permanent Magnet Alloy (Fe-24Co-14Ni-8Al-3Cu)
description: Spinodally decomposed iron-cobalt-nickel-aluminum-copper permanent magnet alloy composed of ferromagnetic Fe-Co-rich BCC α1 nanorods embedded in a weakly magnetic Ni-Al-rich α2 matrix, operating reliably up to 540 °C (Curie temperature ~860 °C). Cubic Im-3m (No. 229), a = 2.878 Å, Z = 2.

name: Kovar Low-Expansion Sealing Alloy (Fe-29Ni-17Co)
description: Controlled thermal-expansion austenitic iron-nickel-cobalt alloy (ASTM F15, CTE ~5.2 × 10⁻⁶ K⁻¹) closely matched to borosilicate glass and alumina ceramics for vacuum-tight glass-to-metal and ceramic-to-metal hermetic feedthroughs. Cubic Fm-3m (No. 225), a = 3.582 Å, Z = 4.

name: Sigma-Phase Cobalt-Chromium Intermetallic (σ-CoCr)
description: Hard, brittle topologically close-packed (TCP) Frank-Kasper tetragonal intermetallic phase (30 atoms/cell) forming in aged Co-Cr alloys near 50–65 at% Cr; its dense multiplet between 42° and 49° 2θ is the primary XRD indicator of embrittling σ-phase precipitation in CoCrMo castings and superalloys. Tetragonal P42/mnm (No. 136), a = 8.772 Å, c = 4.544 Å, Z = 30 atoms, PDF 00-009-0052.

name: Sigma-Phase Iron-Chromium Intermetallic (σ-FeCr)
description: Canonical tetragonal Frank-Kasper TCP intermetallic phase (D8b structure, 30 atoms/cell) precipitating between 600 and 900 °C in duplex, ferritic, and austenitic stainless steels and Cr-Fe alloys, causing severe loss of toughness and pitting resistance. Tetragonal P42/mnm (No. 136), a = 8.7995 Å, c = 4.5442 Å, PDF 00-005-0708.

name: Chromium-Nickel 50/50 Alloy (Cr-50Ni, Dual-Phase BCC+FCC)
description: Eutectic high-chromium corrosion-resistant alloy (ASTM A560 Grade 50Cr-50Ni) combining a Cr-rich BCC α-phase (Im-3m, a = 2.889 Å) and Ni-rich FCC γ-phase (Fm-3m, a = 3.568 Å) for extreme resistance to vanadium-pentoxide and alkali-sulfate fuel-ash corrosion.

name: Ducrolloy Chromium-Iron ODS Alloy (Cr-5Fe-1Y2O3)
description: Powder-metallurgy oxide-dispersion-strengthened (ODS) chromium-base alloy (94Cr-5Fe-1Y2O3) engineered to match the thermal expansion of yttria-stabilized zirconia (YSZ) electrolytes while resisting high-temperature oxidation in planar solid oxide fuel cells (SOFC). Cubic Im-3m (No. 229), a = 2.882 Å, Z = 2.

name: Chromium-Molybdenum Refractory Alloy (Cr-30Mo, BCC)
description: Continuous body-centered cubic solid-solution refractory alloy (70 wt% Cr, 30 wt% Mo) exhibiting lattice expansion relative to pure α-Cr (a = 2.952 Å vs 2.884 Å) and superior high-temperature erosion, creep, and corrosion resistance. Cubic Im-3m (No. 229), a = 2.952 Å, Z = 2.

name: Chromium-Niobium Laves Phase Alloy (Cr2Nb, C15 Cubic)
description: High-melting-point (1730 °C) C15 cubic Laves-phase refractory intermetallic alloy (MgCu2-type) offering exceptional high-temperature strength, low density, and oxidation resistance as the strengthening phase in Cr-Cr2Nb structural alloys. Cubic Fd-3m (No. 227), a = 6.991 Å, Z = 8, PDF 00-047-1638.

name: CrCoNi Medium-Entropy Alloy (Equiatomic CoCrNi MEA)
description: Equiatomic single-phase face-centered cubic chromium-cobalt-nickel medium-entropy alloy (33.3Cr-33.3Co-33.3Ni at%) possessing the highest recorded cryogenic fracture toughness (>500 MPa·m¹/² at 20 K) driven by low stacking-fault energy nanotwinning and HCP nanolath formation. Cubic Fm-3m (No. 225), a = 3.562 Å, Z = 4.

name: Monoclinic Hydroxyapatite (m-HAp, Ordered P21/b Model)
description: Thermodynamically stable, strictly stoichiometric ordered monoclinic model of hydroxyapatite (Elliott 1973), in which OH⁻ dipoles point uniformly along each c-axis channel and alternate in opposite directions between adjacent rows (b = 2a doubling), producing weak diagnostic monoclinic superstructure reflections (131) at 27.09°, (211) at 28.19°, and (150) at 34.29°; transforms reversibly to hexagonal P63/m above ~210 °C. Monoclinic P21/b (No. 14), a = 9.4214 Å, b = 18.8428 Å, c = 6.8814 Å, γ = 120°, Z = 2, PDF 01-089-4405.

name: Oxyhydroxyapatite (OHA, Partially Dehydroxylated HAp Model)
description: Partially dehydroxylated hydroxyapatite model (Ca10(PO4)6(OH)2-2xOx□x, 0 < x < 1) formed during high-temperature sintering (900–1250 °C) and plasma spraying of HAp coatings; hydroxyl vacancy creation expands the c-axis (6.912 Å) and contracts the a-axis (9.406 Å), shifting (002) downward to 25.76° and (300) upward to 32.96°. Hexagonal P63/m (No. 176), a = 9.406 Å, c = 6.912 Å, Z = 1.

name: Oxyapatite (OA, Fully Dehydroxylated Ca10(PO4)6O Model)
description: Anhydrous fully dehydroxylated end-member of the hydroxyapatite thermal series (Ca10(PO4)6O□) formed in vacuum/dry atmospheres at 1050–1350 °C prior to decomposition into TCP + TTCP; shows maximal c-axis elongation (c = 6.930 Å, (002) at 25.69°) and a-axis contraction (a = 9.398 Å). Hexagonal P-6 (No. 174), a = 9.398 Å, c = 6.930 Å, Z = 1, PDF 01-089-6495.

name: Calcium-Deficient Hydroxyapatite (CDHA, Non-Stoichiometric Model)
description: Non-stoichiometric calcium-deficient hydroxyapatite model (Ca10-x(HPO4)x(PO4)6-x(OH)2-x, Ca/P = 1.50–1.61) precipitated by hydrolysis of α-TCP bone cements or low-temperature aqueous synthesis; chemically closest to biological bone mineral and thermally converts to β-TCP (Ca/P = 1.50) or BCP (1.50 < Ca/P < 1.67) above 750 °C. Hexagonal P63/m (No. 176), a = 9.435 Å, c = 6.878 Å, Z = 1.

name: Carbonated Hydroxyapatite (Type-A, Channel CO3²⁻ Model)
description: A-type carbonated hydroxyapatite structural model (Ca10(PO4)6(CO3)x(OH)2-2x) synthesized by dry CO2 annealing at 900–1000 °C, where planar CO3²⁻ ions replace two channel OH⁻ ions along the c-axis; strongly expands the a-axis (9.520 Å) and contracts the c-axis (6.858 Å), shifting (300) downward to 32.56° and (002) upward to 25.96° — directly opposite to Type-B carbonate substitution. Hexagonal P63/m (No. 176), a = 9.520 Å, c = 6.858 Å, Z = 1.

name: Carbonated Hydroxyapatite (Type-AB, Physiological Bone Model)
description: Dual-site AB-type carbonated hydroxyapatite model (4–8 wt% CO3²⁻ occupying both PO4³⁻ B-sites and OH⁻ A-sites with Na⁺/vacancy charge balance), reproducing the exact crystallography and enhanced osteoclastic resorption rate of natural mammalian cortical bone mineral. Hexagonal P63/m (No. 176), a = 9.432 Å, c = 6.890 Å, Z = 1.

name: Magnesium-Substituted Hydroxyapatite (Mg-HAp, 5 mol%)
description: Magnesium-doped biomimetic hydroxyapatite (Ca9.5Mg0.5(PO4)6(OH)2) mimicking the Mg²⁺ content of newly formed osteoid bone; substitution of smaller Mg²⁺ (0.72 Å) for Ca²⁺ (1.00 Å) contracts both a (9.388 Å) and c (6.862 Å), shifting all Bragg peaks to higher 2θ angles and lowering the HAp→β-TCP transition temperature. Hexagonal P63/m (No. 176), Z = 1.

name: Zinc-Substituted Hydroxyapatite (Zn-HAp, 5 mol% Antibacterial)
description: Zinc-doped hydroxyapatite model (Ca9.5Zn0.5(PO4)6(OH)2) providing localized antibacterial protection and enhanced osteoblast proliferation/alkaline-phosphatase activity around orthopedic and dental implants; smaller Zn²⁺ (0.74 Å) contracts the unit cell (a = 9.394 Å, c = 6.868 Å). Hexagonal P63/m (No. 176), Z = 1.

name: Silver-Substituted Hydroxyapatite (Ag-HAp, Antimicrobial Model)
description: Silver-substituted antimicrobial hydroxyapatite model (Ca9.5Ag0.5(PO4)6(OH)1.5) engineered to prevent prosthetic joint biofilm infections (S. aureus, E. coli) via sustained Ag⁺ release; larger Ag⁺ (1.28 Å) expands the hexagonal lattice (a = 9.442 Å, c = 6.898 Å), shifting peaks to slightly lower 2θ angles. Hexagonal P63/m (No. 176), Z = 1.

name: Iron-Substituted Magnetic Hydroxyapatite (Fe-HAp)
description: Intrinsically superparamagnetic Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺-substituted hydroxyapatite model (Ca9.2Fe0.8(PO4)6(OH)2) designed for magnetic bone hyperthermia, MRI T2 contrast imaging, and magnetically guided osteogenic regeneration without secondary iron oxide phases. Hexagonal P63/m (No. 176), a = 9.402 Å, c = 6.872 Å, Z = 1.

name: Monoclinic Chlorapatite (m-ClAp, Ordered P21/b Model)
description: Stoichiometric ordered monoclinic chlorapatite model (Ca10(PO4)6Cl2) in which large Cl⁻ ions sit off the mirror plane in ordered columns along c (b = 2a), markedly expanding a (9.628 Å) and contracting c (6.764 Å) relative to HAp/FAp so (002) shifts up to 26.33° while (221) shifts down to 31.29°. Monoclinic P21/b (No. 14), a = 9.628 Å, b = 19.256 Å, c = 6.764 Å, γ = 120°, Z = 2, PDF 01-070-1880.

name: Alpha-Prime Tricalcium Phosphate (α'-TCP, Super-α Hexagonal Polymorph)
description: Highest-temperature glaserite-type hexagonal polymorph of tricalcium phosphate (α'-Ca3(PO4)2), thermodynamically stable between 1430 °C and melting at 1756 °C (and stabilized at room temperature by SiO4⁴⁻/BO3³⁻ doping); serves as the high-symmetry aristotype parent structure of monoclinic α-TCP. Hexagonal P63/mmc (No. 194), a = 5.3507 Å, c = 7.684 Å, Z = 1, PDF 04-010-4348.

name: Gamma-Tricalcium Phosphate (γ-TCP, High-Pressure Tuite Polymorph)
description: Dense high-pressure polymorph of tricalcium phosphate (mineral name Tuite, Ba3(PO4)2-type structure) synthesized above 4 GPa and 1000 °C or found in shocked meteorites and mantle inclusions; 12% denser than β-TCP (3.45 vs 3.07 g/cm³) with centrosymmetric rhombohedral symmetry. Rhombohedral R-3m (No. 166), a = 5.249 Å, c = 18.674 Å, Z = 3, PDF 01-070-2065.

name: Silicon-Stabilized Alpha-Tricalcium Phosphate (Si-α-TCP)
description: Silicate-substituted α-tricalcium phosphate bioceramic (Ca3(PO4)1.9(SiO4)0.1) in which SiO4⁴⁻ stabilizes the bioactive α-TCP polymorph at lower sintering temperatures while accelerating apatite layer nucleation and osteoblast differentiation in vivo. Monoclinic P21/a (No. 14), a = 12.898 Å, b = 27.295 Å, c = 15.232 Å, β = 126.18°, Z = 24.

name: Zinc-Substituted Beta-Tricalcium Phosphate (Zn-β-TCP, 5 mol%)
description: Zinc-doped β-tricalcium phosphate (Ca2.85Zn0.15(PO4)2) in which Zn²⁺ preferentially occupies the octahedral Ca(5) site, contracting the R3c lattice (a = 10.398 Å, c = 37.310 Å), raising the β→α transformation temperature above 1300 °C, and releasing osteostimulatory/antibacterial Zn²⁺ ions during resorption. Rhombohedral R3c (No. 161), Z = 21.

name: Synthetic Magnesium Whitlockite (Ca18Mg2(HPO4)2(PO4)12, Bone Second Mineral)
description: True hydrated acidic magnesium whitlockite (Ca18Mg2(HPO4)2(PO4)12), the second most abundant inorganic mineral phase in human bone (~20 wt% of bone mineral) and dental calculus; distinguished from anhydrous β-TCP by its markedly contracted lattice (a = 10.350 Å, c = 37.085 Å) shifting the main (0210) reflection up to 31.28°. Rhombohedral R3c (No. 161), Z = 3, PDF 01-070-2064.

name: Biphasic Calcium Phosphate BCP 20/80 (20% HAp / 80% β-TCP Fast-Resorbing)
description: β-TCP-dominant biphasic calcium phosphate (20 wt% HAp / 80 wt% β-TCP) engineered for rapid osteoclastic resorption and fast vascularized bone ingrowth in sinus-lift and cancellous defect grafting, where β-TCP (0210) at 31.01° dominates over HAp (211) at 31.78°.

name: Triphasic Calcium Phosphate (HAp / β-TCP / α-TCP High-Temp Sintered)
