description: Triphasic calcium phosphate reference assemblage containing hexagonal HAp (P63/m), rhombohedral β-TCP (R3c), and monoclinic α-TCP (P21/a), characteristic of thermally decomposed HAp sintered above 1150–1250 °C and plasma-sprayed bioceramic coatings; enables simultaneous identification of 30.71° (α-TCP), 31.01° (β-TCP), and 31.78° (HAp).

name: Beta-Calcium Pyrophosphate (β-CPP, β-Ca2P2O7 Sintering Byproduct)
description: Tetragonal low-temperature polymorph of anhydrous calcium pyrophosphate (β-Ca2P2O7, Ca/P = 1.00) forming as the primary diagnostic impurity phase whenever Ca/P < 1.50 during β-TCP or HAp sintering (750–1140 °C); also used directly as a bioactive bone-substitute ceramic. Tetragonal P41 (No. 76), a = 6.685 Å, c = 24.147 Å, Z = 8, PDF 00-009-0346.

name: Alpha-Calcium Pyrophosphate (α-CPP, α-Ca2P2O7 High-Temp Polymorph)
description: High-temperature monoclinic polymorph of calcium pyrophosphate (α-Ca2P2O7) formed above 1140 °C from β-CPP in Ca-deficient TCP/HAp syntheses and phosphate glass-ceramics. Monoclinic P21/n (No. 14), a = 12.660 Å, b = 8.542 Å, c = 5.315 Å, β = 90.30°, Z = 4, PDF 00-009-0345.

name: ZIRLO Nuclear Cladding Alloy (Zr-1Nb-1Sn-0.1Fe)
description: Advanced niobium-tin-iron zirconium nuclear cladding alloy (Westinghouse ZIRLO / Optimized ZIRLO: Zr-1.0Nb-1.0Sn-0.1Fe) offering superior waterside corrosion resistance, low irradiation growth, and reduced hydrogen pickup for high-burnup (>60 GWd/MTU) PWR cores. Hexagonal P63/mmc (No. 194), a = 3.230 Å, c = 5.146 Å, Z = 2.

name: M5 / E110 Nuclear Cladding Alloy (Zr-1Nb-0.13O)
description: Tin-free binary zirconium-1 wt% niobium nuclear fuel cladding alloy (Framatome M5 / VVER E110, recrystallized α-Zr matrix with fine dispersed β-Nb precipitates), delivering exceptional resistance to breakaway oxidation and very low hydrogen pickup fraction. Hexagonal P63/mmc (No. 194), a = 3.232 Å, c = 5.150 Å, Z = 2.

name: Zr-2.5Nb Alloy (CANDU Pressure Tube & Oxinium Biomedical Alloy)
description: Dual-phase α+β zirconium-2.5 wt% niobium alloy consisting of elongated HCP α-Zr grains (P63/mmc, a = 3.230 Å, c = 5.146 Å) bordered by continuous Nb-enriched BCC β-Zr filaments (~20 wt% Nb, Im-3m, a = 3.555 Å); flagship alloy for CANDU heavy-water reactor pressure tubes and oxidized-zirconium (Oxinium) hip/knee joint prostheses.

name: E635 Nuclear Cladding Alloy (Zr-1.2Sn-1Nb-0.35Fe)
description: Multicomponent quaternary zirconium-tin-niobium-iron alloy (Zr-1.2Sn-1.0Nb-0.35Fe) engineered for VVER fuel assembly guide channels and rigid skeleton components with exceptionally low irradiation-induced creep and axial growth. Hexagonal P63/mmc (No. 194), a = 3.229 Å, c = 5.147 Å, Z = 2.

name: Zr-4.5Nb-1.5Sn (High-Strength Dual-Phase Nuclear Alloy)
description: High-strength α+β zirconium-niobium-tin structural alloy (Excel-class Zr-4.5Nb-1.5Sn) combining solution-strengthened HCP α-Zr (a = 3.228 Å, c = 5.144 Å) with retained BCC β-Zr (a = 3.545 Å) for Gen-IV supercritical water-cooled reactor (SCWR) pressure tubes.

name: Zirconium 702 (UNS R60702, Commercially Pure Chemical Grade)
description: Commercial-purity unalloyed zirconium (ASTM B551 Grade 702, ≥99.2% Zr+Hf, ≤4.5% Hf) serving as the standard corrosion-resistant structural metal for hot hydrochloric, sulfuric, acetic, and nitric acid chemical process equipment. Hexagonal P63/mmc (No. 194), a = 3.232 Å, c = 5.148 Å, Z = 2.

name: Zirconium 705 (UNS R60705, Zr-2.5Nb Chemical Process Alloy)
description: High-strength commercial chemical-grade zirconium-2.5 wt% niobium alloy (ASTM B551 Grade 705, ≤4.5% Hf) offering nearly double the yield strength of Zr702 while maintaining weldability and acid resistance via dual-phase α-Zr + β-Zr (a_β = 3.552 Å) microstructure.

name: Zr-12Nb-4Sn (Biomedical Low-Modulus β-Zirconium Alloy)
description: Nickel- and vanadium-free metastable β-zirconium biomedical implant alloy (Zr-12Nb-4Sn) combining bone-matched low Young's modulus (~52 GPa), superelasticity, and ultra-low magnetic susceptibility (~1.2 × 10⁻⁶ cm³/g) to eliminate MRI imaging artifacts around orthopedic/vascular implants. Cubic Im-3m (No. 229), a = 3.536 Å, Z = 2.

name: Zr-14Nb (Biomedical Metastable β-Zirconium Implant Alloy)
description: Binary metastable body-centered cubic β-zirconium-14 wt% niobium biomedical alloy exhibiting minimal magnetic susceptibility (~1.1 × 10⁻⁶ cm³/g — less than one-third that of Ti-6Al-4V) and low elastic modulus (~58 GPa) for neurosurgical clips and spinal instrumentation. Cubic Im-3m (No. 229), a = 3.528 Å, Z = 2.

name: Zr-1Mo (Biomedical Low-Susceptibility α-Zirconium Alloy)
description: Dilute molybdenum-alloyed HCP zirconium biomedical alloy (Zr-1 wt% Mo) engineered specifically for minimum magnetic susceptibility in 3T/7T high-field MRI scanners while retaining high corrosion resistance and osseointegration. Hexagonal P63/mmc (No. 194), a = 3.226 Å, c = 5.140 Å, Z = 2.

name: Zr-20Ti (HCP Biomedical & Dental Solid-Solution Alloy)
description: Single-phase HCP zirconium-20 wt% titanium solid-solution alloy combining superior mechanical strength, low elastic modulus (~78 GPa), and complete biological inertness; Ti addition contracts the α-Zr cell (a = 3.168 Å, c = 5.048 Å), shifting (101) from 36.52° to 37.27°. Hexagonal P63/mmc (No. 194), Z = 2.

name: Zr-50Ti (Equiatomic TiZr / Roxolid-Class Dental Implant Alloy)
description: Complete-solid-solution binary hexagonal zirconium-titanium alloy (50 wt% Zr / 50 wt% Ti) exhibiting maximal solid-solution strengthening, high fatigue endurance, and Vegard-interpolated lattice parameters (a = 3.092 Å, c = 4.918 Å) midway between α-Zr and α-Ti. Hexagonal P63/mmc (No. 194), Z = 2.

name: B2-ZrCu Shape-Memory & BMG Composite Phase (Zr50Cu50)
description: Ordered CsCl-type (B2) cubic parent austenite phase of equiatomic zirconium-copper (ZrCu), critical both as a high-temperature shape-memory alloy (Ms ~140 °C, B2 ↔ B19') and as the ductile transformation-induced-plasticity (TRIP) crystalline reinforcement inside Zr-Cu-Al bulk metallic glass composites (BMGCs). Cubic Pm-3m (No. 221), a = 3.262 Å, Z = 1, PDF 01-071-8347.

name: Zr2Cu Intermetallic (C11b Tetragonal BMG Devitrification Phase)
description: Body-centered tetragonal MoSi2-type (C11b) zirconium-copper intermetallic (Zr2Cu), the primary crystalline devitrification product formed upon annealing Zr-Cu-Ni-Al (Vitreloy-class) bulk metallic glasses above their crystallization temperature. Tetragonal I4/mmm (No. 139), a = 3.220 Å, c = 11.183 Å, Z = 2, PDF 00-018-0466.

name: Zr(Fe,Cr)2 Laves Precipitate (C14 Hexagonal Zircaloy SPP)
description: Hexagonal MgZn2-type (C14) Laves intermetallic precipitate (Zr(Fe,Cr)2) forming the primary corrosion- and hydrogen-pickup-controlling second-phase particles (SPPs) in Zircaloy-2 and Zircaloy-4 nuclear fuel cladding; its dissolution/amorphization under neutron irradiation governs high-burnup cladding life. Hexagonal P63/mmc (No. 194), a = 5.042 Å, c = 8.234 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-042-1289.

name: ZrCr2 Laves Phase Alloy (C15 Cubic Hydrogen-Storage Intermetallic)
description: Cubic MgCu2-type (C15) AB2 Laves-phase intermetallic (ZrCr2) serving as a benchmark solid-state hydrogen-storage alloy (absorbing up to ZrCr2H3.6) and Ni-MH negative electrode material, as well as the chromium-rich end-member of Zircaloy Laves precipitates. Cubic Fd-3m (No. 227), a = 7.207 Å, Z = 8, PDF 00-006-0612.

name: Zr2Ni Intermetallic (C16 Tetragonal Zircaloy-2 & Hydrogen-Storage Phase)
description: Body-centered tetragonal CuAl2-type (C16) intermetallic (Zr2Ni / Zr2(Fe,Ni)) forming the secondary Ni-bearing precipitate in Zircaloy-2 BWR cladding and an important devitrification/hydrogenation phase in Zr-Ni metallic glasses. Tetragonal I4/mcm (No. 140), a = 6.483 Å, c = 5.267 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-038-1170.

name: Delta-Zirconium Hydride (δ-ZrH1.66, FCC Nuclear Cladding Embrittlement Phase)
description: Face-centered cubic CaF2-type (fluorite) zirconium hydride (δ-ZrH1.66, H/Zr = 1.5–1.7), the predominant brittle hydride phase precipitating as platelets inside Zircaloy-2/4, ZIRLO, M5, and Zr-2.5Nb nuclear fuel cladding and pressure tubes; its diagnostic (111) peak at 32.42° directly adjacent to α-Zr (100) at 31.95° is used worldwide to quantify Delayed Hydride Cracking (DHC) risk. Cubic Fm-3m (No. 225), a = 4.779 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-034-0649.

name: Gamma-Zirconium Hydride (γ-ZrH, FCT Metastable Cladding Hydride)
description: Metastable face-centered tetragonal (FCT, c/a = 1.081) ordered zirconium monohydride (γ-ZrH) precipitating as fine needles during fast cooling of hydrogen-charged α-Zr and Zircaloy cladding; distinguished from cubic δ-ZrH1.66 by the tetragonal splitting of (002)/(200) at 36.12° and 39.17°. Tetragonal P42/n (No. 86), FCT cell a = 4.596 Å, c = 4.969 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-034-0690.

name: Mixed Oxide Nuclear Fuel (MOX, U0.80Pu0.20O2)
description: Solid-solution fluorite mixed uranium-plutonium oxide nuclear fuel (U0.80Pu0.20O2, 20 mol% PuO2 in UO2) obeying Vegard's law between UO2 (5.4704 Å) and PuO2 (5.3960 Å), deployed in commercial LWRs and fast-spectrum reactors. Cubic Fm-3m (No. 225), a = 5.4555 Å, Z = 4, PDF 01-089-4940.

name: Uranium Tetrafluoride (UF4, Green Salt)
description: Crystalline emerald-green uranium tetrafluoride (UF4, 'green salt'), the key non-volatile solid intermediate between uranium oxides, uranium metal reduction, UF6 conversion, and molten-salt reactor (MSR) fuel salts. Monoclinic C2/c (No. 15), a = 12.803 Å, b = 10.792 Å, c = 8.372 Å, β = 126.3°, Z = 12, PDF 00-032-1401.

name: Uranium Hexafluoride (UF6, Crystalline Solid)
description: Room-temperature orthorhombic molecular crystal of uranium hexafluoride (UF6) composed of discrete octahedral UF6 molecules; sublimes at 56.5 °C and is the standard feedstock of commercial uranium isotope processing. Orthorhombic Pnma (No. 62), a = 9.900 Å, b = 8.962 Å, c = 5.207 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-009-0166.

name: Beta-Uranium Hydride (β-UH3)
description: Equilibrium cubic A15-type beta-uranium trihydride (β-UH3), a ferromagnetic, pyrophoric powder formed by direct reaction of uranium metal with hydrogen gas; crucial in spent metallic fuel storage safety and hydrogen/tritium isotope storage beds. Cubic Pm-3n (No. 223), a = 6.645 Å, Z = 8, PDF 00-012-0435.

name: Uranium Dicarbide (α-UC2, Tetragonal TRISO Fuel Phase)
description: Body-centered tetragonal CaC2-type uranium dicarbide (α-UC2), a refractory carbide phase occurring inside high-temperature gas-cooled reactor (HTGR) TRISO UCO fuel kernels with carbon-carbon dumbbells along the c-axis. Tetragonal I4/mmm (No. 139), a = 3.517 Å, c = 5.987 Å, Z = 2, PDF 00-006-0372.

name: U-10Mo Monolithic Nuclear Fuel Alloy (γ-U-10wt%Mo)
description: Metastable body-centered cubic gamma-stabilized uranium–10 wt% molybdenum (γ-U-10Mo) monolithic low-enriched uranium (LEU) fuel alloy engineered to convert high-performance research reactors from HEU to LEU with isotropic irradiation swelling resistance. Cubic Im-3m (No. 229), a = 3.417 Å, Z = 2, PDF 01-089-4941.

name: Uranium Oxide Hyperstoichiometric (U4O9, β-U4O9)
description: Ordered interstitial-oxygen fluorite superstructure phase (U4O9 / UO2.25) formed during air oxidation of UO2 spent nuclear fuel; exhibits a contracted fluorite subcell (a = 5.441 Å, 4×4×4 cuboctahedral oxygen-cluster supercell) relative to stoichiometric UO2 (5.4704 Å). Cubic I-43d (No. 220), subcell a = 5.441 Å, PDF 00-020-1344.

name: Uranium Peroxide Tetrahydrate (Studtite, UO4·4H2O)
description: Naturally occurring and radiolysis-induced uranyl peroxide mineral studtite ([(UO2)(O2)(H2O)2]·2H2O), forming on spent nuclear fuel surfaces exposed to water via alpha-radiolysis H2O2 generation and used in yellowcake peroxide precipitation. Monoclinic C2/c (No. 15), a = 14.068 Å, b = 6.721 Å, c = 8.428 Å, β = 123.35°, Z = 4, PDF 00-049-1821.

name: Uranyl Nitrate Hexahydrate (UNH, UO2(NO3)2·6H2O)
description: Yellow-green fluorescent orthorhombic uranyl nitrate hexahydrate (UNH), the principal water-soluble uranium salt produced in PUREX spent fuel reprocessing and uranium refining prior to thermal denitration to UO3. Orthorhombic Cmc21 (No. 36), a = 13.197 Å, b = 8.035 Å, c = 11.467 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-031-1436.

name: Autunite (Ca(UO2)2(PO4)2·10H2O, Secondary Uranium Mineral)
description: Bright yellow-green strongly UV-fluorescent layered uranyl phosphate mineral autunite (Ca(UO2)2(PO4)2·10–12H2O), a major secondary uranium ore characterized by its intense 10.33 Å basal (002) reflection at 8.55° 2θ. Tetragonal pseudo-cell I4/mmm (No. 139), a = 7.00 Å, c = 20.67 Å, Z = 2, PDF 00-041-1353.

name: Carnotite (K2(UO2)2(VO4)2·3H2O, Uranium-Vanadium Ore)
description: Canary-yellow layered potassium uranyl vanadate mineral carnotite (K2(UO2)2(VO4)2·3H2O), a classic Colorado Plateau sandstone-hosted uranium and vanadium ore mineral with diagnostic 6.40 Å basal (001) spacing at 13.83° 2θ. Monoclinic P21/a (No. 14), a = 10.47 Å, b = 8.41 Å, c = 6.59 Å, β = 103.8°, Z = 2, PDF 00-008-0317.

name: Delta-Prime Plutonium (δ'-Pu, Body-Centered Tetragonal)
description: Body-centered tetragonal (BCT) fifth solid allotrope of plutonium (δ'-Pu, stable in a narrow temperature window 452–480 °C between FCC δ-Pu and BCC ε-Pu) with extreme negative thermal expansion along the c-axis. Tetragonal I4/mmm (No. 139), a = 3.3261 Å, c = 4.4630 Å, Z = 2, PDF 01-089-4932.

name: Epsilon-Plutonium (ε-Pu, High-Temperature BCC Phase)
description: High-temperature body-centered cubic sixth solid allotrope of plutonium (ε-Pu, stable from 480 °C up to its 640 °C melting point), showing rapid self-diffusion and positive volume contraction upon melting. Cubic Im-3m (No. 229), a = 3.6361 Å, Z = 2, PDF 01-089-4933.

name: Delta-Stabilized Plutonium-Gallium Alloy (δ-Pu-1wt%Ga)
description: Room-temperature FCC δ-stabilized plutonium–1 wt% (~3.3 at%) gallium solid-solution alloy; Ga substitution contracts the FCC lattice from 4.6371 Å to 4.614 Å, suppressing the brittle δ→α' martensitic transformation and yielding ductile isotropic metallurgy. Cubic Fm-3m (No. 225), a = 4.614 Å, Z = 4, PDF 01-089-4942.

name: Plutonium Sesquioxide (α-Pu2O3, Hexagonal A-Type)
description: Hexagonal/trigonal La2O3 A-type trivalent plutonium sesquioxide (β/A-Pu2O3), formed by carbothermic or hydrogen reduction of PuO2 under low oxygen potential; key reduced phase in high-temperature MOX fuel chemistry. Trigonal P-3m1 (No. 164), a = 3.841 Å, c = 5.958 Å, Z = 1, PDF 00-006-0328.

name: Plutonium Mononitride (PuN, Fast-Reactor Nitride Fuel)
description: Rocksalt-type plutonium mononitride (PuN), an advanced Generation IV fast-reactor and minor-actinide burner nitride fuel component (commonly solid-solutioned with UN or ZrN) offering high heavy-metal density and thermal conductivity. Cubic Fm-3m (No. 225), a = 4.905 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-006-0468.

name: Plutonium Hydride (PuH2, Cubic Fluorite Phase)
description: Face-centered cubic fluorite-structured plutonium dihydride (PuH2.0–2.7), a pyrophoric corrosion product formed rapidly when plutonium metal reacts with hydrogen or moisture; critically monitored in plutonium storage safety and hydriding-dehydriding recycling. Cubic Fm-3m (No. 225), a = 5.359 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-009-0174.

name: Plutonium Tetrafluoride (PuF4)
description: Pink-brown monoclinic plutonium tetrafluoride (PuF4), isostructural with UF4 and ThF4 (ZrF4-type), used in pyrochemical processing, fluorination chemistry, and molten-salt actinide fuel studies. Monoclinic C2/c (No. 15), a = 12.59 Å, b = 10.57 Å, c = 8.28 Å, β = 126.2°, Z = 12, PDF 00-015-0545.

name: Plutonium Trifluoride (PuF3)
description: Violet-purple tysonite-type (LaF3-type) plutonium trifluoride (PuF3), an insoluble trivalent actinide fluoride precipitated from aqueous reprocessing streams and studied in molten-salt actinide burner fuel mixtures. Trigonal P-3c1 (No. 165), a = 7.093 Å, c = 7.254 Å, Z = 6, PDF 00-006-0325.

name: Beta-Neptunium (β-Np, Tetragonal Polymorph)
description: Intermediate-temperature tetragonal allotrope of neptunium metal (β-Np, stable 280–577 °C) with 4 atoms per unit cell formed from alternating planar and puckered layers. Tetragonal P4212 (No. 90), a = 4.897 Å, c = 3.388 Å, Z = 4, PDF 01-089-4934.

name: Gamma-Neptunium (γ-Np, High-Temperature BCC Polymorph)
description: High-temperature body-centered cubic allotrope of neptunium metal (γ-Np, stable 577–644 °C up to melting), forming complete BCC solid solutions with γ-U and ε-Pu in metallic fast-reactor transmutation fuels. Cubic Im-3m (No. 229), a = 3.520 Å, Z = 2, PDF 01-089-4935.

name: Neptunium Dioxide (NpO2, Fluorite Oxide)
description: Olive-green fluorite-type neptunium dioxide (NpO2), the primary stable solid storage form of Np-237 and irradiation target for Pu-238 production for deep-space RTG missions; exhibits exotic multipolar order below 25 K. Cubic Fm-3m (No. 225), a = 5.4334 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-041-1169.

name: Dineptunium Pentoxide (Np2O5)
description: Dark-brown pentavalent neptunium oxide (Np2O5), the highest stable binary oxide of neptunium containing linear neptunyl (NpO2+) cation-cation interaction chains; key solubility-limiting alteration phase in geological nuclear waste repositories. Monoclinic P2/c (No. 13), a = 8.168 Å, b = 6.584 Å, c = 9.313 Å, β = 116.09°, Z = 4, PDF 01-075-1848.

name: Neptunium Mononitride (NpN, Minor-Actinide Transmutation Fuel)
description: Rocksalt-type neptunium mononitride (NpN), an itinerant-5f ferromagnetic refractory actinide nitride studied for Accelerator-Driven System (ADS) and fast-reactor minor-actinide transmutation fuels. Cubic Fm-3m (No. 225), a = 4.897 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-010-0263.

name: Neptunium Monocarbide (NpC)
description: Rocksalt-type neptunium monocarbide (NpC1-x), a refractory actinide carbide exhibiting ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic transitions and complete miscibility with UC and PuC in fast-reactor carbide fuels. Cubic Fm-3m (No. 225), a = 5.004 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-015-0895.

name: Beta-Thorium (β-Th, High-Temperature BCC Polymorph)
description: High-temperature body-centered cubic allotrope of thorium metal (β-Th, stable from 1360 °C to its 1755 °C melting point). Cubic Im-3m (No. 229), a = 4.110 Å, Z = 2, PDF 01-089-4936.

name: Thorium Mononitride (ThN)
description: Golden-yellow metallic rocksalt-type thorium mononitride (ThN), a superconducting (Tc ≈ 3.2 K), ultra-refractory (mp 2820 °C) fertile nitride fuel candidate for fast-spectrum thorium breeder reactors. Cubic Fm-3m (No. 225), a = 5.159 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-015-0035.

name: Thorium Tetrafluoride (ThF4, Molten-Salt Reactor Breeder Salt)
description: White monoclinic thorium tetrafluoride (ThF4, ZrF4 structure type), the primary fertile thorium component dissolved in LiF–BeF2 (FLiBe) liquid-fuel Molten Salt Breeder Reactors (MSBRs) and used in specialized IR optical coatings. Monoclinic C2/c (No. 15), a = 13.00 Å, b = 10.99 Å, c = 8.60 Å, β = 126.4°, Z = 12, PDF 00-023-1426.

name: Thorite (ThSiO4, Tetragonal Thorium Silicate Mineral)
description: Zircon-type tetragonal thorium orthosilicate mineral thorite (ThSiO4), a primary accessory thorium-uranium ore mineral in granitic pegmatites and studied as a durable actinide-immobilization ceramic host. Tetragonal I41/amd (No. 141), a = 7.1328 Å, c = 6.3188 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-011-0419.

name: Alpha-Protactinium Metal (α-Pa, Body-Centered Tetragonal)
description: Room-temperature body-centered tetragonal (BCT) allotrope of protactinium (α-Pa, element 91, Z = 2, c/a = 0.825), the first actinide exhibiting itinerant 5f-electron bonding and superconductivity (Tc = 1.4 K). Tetragonal I4/mmm (No. 139), a = 3.925 Å, c = 3.238 Å, Z = 2, PDF 00-009-0231.

name: Protactinium Dioxide (PaO2, Fluorite Oxide)
description: Black face-centered cubic fluorite-type protactinium dioxide (PaO2), formed by hydrogen reduction of Pa2O5 at 1550 °C; bridges ThO2 (5.5974 Å) and UO2 (5.4704 Å) in the actinide dioxide contraction series. Cubic Fm-3m (No. 225), a = 5.505 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-006-0523.

name: Actinium Metal (Ac, FCC Actinide Series Head)
description: Silvery-white radioactive face-centered cubic actinium metal (Ac, element 89, parent of the actinide series), glowing pale blue in air from Cherenkov/air-ionization luminescence; Ac-225 is a leading targeted alpha-therapy (TAT) medical radioisotope. Cubic Fm-3m (No. 225), a = 5.311 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-016-0469.

name: Alpha-Americium Metal (α-Am, Double Hexagonal Close-Packed)
description: Room-temperature double hexagonal close-packed (DHCP, ABAC stacking) allotrope of americium metal (α-Am, element 95), marking the onset of localized lanthanide-like 5f electrons in the transplutonium actinides and becoming superconducting at 0.79 K. Hexagonal P63/mmc (No. 194), a = 3.4681 Å, c = 11.241 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-017-0180.

name: Alpha-Curium Metal (α-Cm, Double Hexagonal Close-Packed)
description: Room-temperature double hexagonal close-packed (DHCP) allotrope of curium metal (α-Cm, element 96), characterized by a half-filled 5f7 magnetic shell (antiferromagnetic below 65 K) and strong alpha-decay self-heating (Cm-244). Hexagonal P63/mmc (No. 194), a = 3.496 Å, c = 11.331 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-017-0181.

name: Curium Dioxide (CmO2, Fluorite Radioisotope Heat-Source Oxide)
description: Black cubic fluorite-structured curium dioxide (CmO2), formed by heating curium oxalate or hydroxide in oxygen; exhibits measurable radiation self-swelling of its lattice parameter from alpha recoil damage. Cubic Fm-3m (No. 225), a = 5.359 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-016-0468.

name: Alpha-Berkelium Metal (α-Bk, DHCP Transplutonium Actinide)
description: Room-temperature double hexagonal close-packed (DHCP) allotrope of berkelium metal (α-Bk, element 97, Bk-249), a trivalent heavy actinide used as the target material for synthesizing superheavy elements such as Tennessine (Z = 117). Hexagonal P63/mmc (No. 194), a = 3.416 Å, c = 11.069 Å, Z = 4, PDF 01-089-4937.

name: Alpha-Californium Metal (α-Cf, DHCP Neutron-Source Actinide)
description: Room-temperature double hexagonal close-packed (DHCP) allotrope of californium metal (α-Cf, element 98), the heaviest actinide produced in weighable quantities; Cf-252 is a premier spontaneous-fission neutron source for reactor startup, radiography, and prompt-gamma activation analysis. Hexagonal P63/mmc (No. 194), a = 3.384 Å, c = 11.040 Å, Z = 4, PDF 01-089-4938.

name: Radium Metal (Ra, Radioactive Alkaline-Earth BCC Metal)
description: Silvery-white body-centered cubic radioactive alkaline-earth metal (Ra, element 88, isostructural with barium); Ra-223 dichloride is utilized clinically in targeted alpha radiotherapy for metastatic bone cancer. Cubic Im-3m (No. 229), a = 5.148 Å, Z = 2, PDF 00-012-0301.

name: Radium Sulfate (RaSO4, Orthorhombic Barite-Type Salt)
description: Insoluble orthorhombic barite-type radium sulfate (RaSO4), the least water-soluble sulfate salt known (Ksp ≈ 10^-10.3), forming solid solutions with BaSO4 in oilfield NORM scales and uranium mill tailings remediation. Orthorhombic Pnma (No. 62), a = 9.126 Å, b = 5.540 Å, c = 7.313 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-039-1468.

name: Promethium Sesquioxide (Pm2O3, Cubic C-Type Radioactive Lanthanide)
description: Pale-pink body-centered cubic C-type bixbyite promethium(III) oxide (C-Pm2O3, element 61, the only purely radioactive lanthanide); Pm-147 is a pure beta emitter used in betavoltaic nuclear micro-batteries and luminous phosphors. Cubic Ia-3 (No. 206), a = 10.990 Å, Z = 16, PDF 00-026-1356.

name: Zamak 5 (Zinc Die-Casting Alloy, Zn-4Al-1Cu-0.04Mg)
description: Copper-strengthened zinc die-casting alloy Zamak 5 (ASTM AC41A, Zn-4wt%Al-1wt%Cu-0.04wt%Mg) offering higher hardness, tensile strength, and creep resistance than Zamak 3. Primary HCP η-Zn matrix (P63/mmc, a = 2.665 Å, c = 4.947 Å) with FCC α-Al eutectic reflections (38.52°, 44.77°).

name: ZA-8 (Zinc-Aluminum Foundry Alloy, Zn-8.4Al-1Cu)
description: Hot-chamber die-castable hypereutectic zinc-aluminum alloy ZA-8 (Zn-8.4wt%Al-1.0wt%Cu-0.02wt%Mg) with higher strength and bearing wear resistance than Zamak grades. Dual-phase HCP η-Zn (P63/mmc) + FCC α-Al (Fm-3m) dendritic microstructure.

name: ZA-27 (High-Strength Zinc-Aluminum Alloy, Zn-27Al-2Cu)
description: Highest-strength commercial zinc-aluminum alloy ZA-27 (Zn-27wt%Al-2.2wt%Cu-0.015wt%Mg), rivaling cast iron and bronze in load-bearing bushings and gears. Dual-phase HCP η-Zn (P63/mmc, 43.22° (101)) and prominent FCC α-Al solid solution (Fm-3m, 38.52° (111), 44.77° (200)).

name: Beta-Brass (CuZn, Ordered B2 CsCl-Type Phase)
description: Archetypal Hume-Rothery 3/2 electron compound β'-CuZn crystallizing in the ordered B2 (CsCl-type) body-centered cubic structure below 468 °C (diagnostic superlattice (100) at 30.23° and (111) at 53.70°). Basis for shape-memory Cu-Zn-Al alloys and high-strength duplex brasses. Cubic Pm-3m (No. 221), a = 2.9539 Å, Z = 1, PDF 00-002-1231.

name: Gamma-Brass (Cu5Zn8, Complex Cubic Electron Compound)
description: Classic Hume-Rothery 21/13 electron compound γ-Cu5Zn8 containing 52 atoms per unit cell in a complex 26-atom cluster body-centered cubic superstructure. Hard, brittle intermetallic phase important in Cu-Zn diffusion couples, soldering interfaces, and brass metallurgy. Cubic I-43m (No. 217), a = 8.8690 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-025-1228.

name: Muntz Metal (C28000, Alpha-Beta Brass Cu60Zn40)
description: Classic duplex alpha-beta brass (Muntz Metal UNS C28000, Cu-40wt%Zn) combining ductile FCC α-Cu(Zn) (a = 3.698 Å, (111) at 42.30°) with high-strength ordered BCC β'-CuZn (a = 2.954 Å, (110) at 43.28°). Widely used for marine condenser tube sheets, hot forgings, and architectural trim. Cubic Fm-3m + Pm-3m.

name: Galvanized Steel Zeta Phase (ζ-FeZn13, Hot-Dip Coating Intermetallic)
description: Outermost Fe-Zn intermetallic layer (ζ-FeZn13, ~5–6 wt% Fe) formed during hot-dip galvanizing and galvannealing of automotive steel sheets. Monoclinic C2/m (No. 12), a = 13.424 Å, b = 7.608 Å, c = 5.061 Å, β = 127.30°, Z = 2, PDF 00-034-1314.

name: Galvanized Steel Gamma Phase (Γ-Fe3Zn10, Interface Intermetallic)
description: Iron-rich γ-brass-type interfacial intermetallic layer (Γ-Fe3Zn10, 21–28 wt% Fe) nucleating directly adjacent to the steel substrate during hot-dip galvannealing; excessive Γ thickness causes powdering/flaking during press forming. Cubic I-43m (No. 217), a = 8.982 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-032-0478.

name: Galvanized Steel Delta Phase (δ-FeZn10, Hexagonal Intermetallic)
description: Primary palisade/compact intermediate Fe-Zn intermetallic layer (δ-FeZn10, 7–11.5 wt% Fe) dominating well-formed galvannealed automotive steel coatings due to its favorable formability and paintability. Large-cell hexagonal P63mc (No. 186), a = 12.787 Å, c = 57.222 Å, PDF 00-045-1184.

name: Biodegradable Zinc-Magnesium Alloy (Zn-1Mg, Zn + Mg2Zn11 Eutectic)
description: Next-generation biodegradable vascular stent and orthopedic fixation alloy (Zn-1wt%Mg) exhibiting an ideal physiological corrosion rate (~0.02–0.1 mm/yr without H2 gas pockets) and doubled strength via HCP η-Zn dendrites reinforced by cubic Mg2Zn11 eutectic intermetallics. Hexagonal P63/mmc + Cubic Pm-3.

name: Magnesium-Zinc Laves Phase (MgZn2, C14 Strengthening Precipitate)
description: Archetypal hexagonal C14 Laves phase (η-MgZn2), the principal age-hardening strengthening precipitate in both wrought Mg-Zn alloys (ZK60) and aerospace 7xxx-series Al-Zn-Mg(-Cu) alloys (7075-T6). Hexagonal P63/mmc (No. 194), a = 5.2210 Å, c = 8.5670 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-034-0457.

name: Zinc-Magnesium Intermetallic (Mg2Zn11, Cubic Eutectic Phase)
description: Primitive cubic zinc-rich intermetallic Mg2Zn11 forming the strengthening eutectic network in biodegradable Zn-Mg alloys and high-corrosion-resistance Zn-Al-Mg (ZAM) steel coatings. Cubic Pm-3 (No. 200), a = 8.5520 Å, Z = 3, PDF 00-006-0664.

name: Zinc Hydroxide (ε-Zn(OH)2, Wülfingite)
description: Thermodynamically stable orthorhombic polymorph of zinc hydroxide (ε-Zn(OH)2, mineral wülfingite) with corner-sharing Zn(OH)4 tetrahedra. Key discharge/passivation product on alkaline Zn-air and aqueous zinc-ion battery anodes and atmospheric Zn corrosion films. Orthorhombic P212121 (No. 19), a = 4.920 Å, b = 5.162 Å, c = 8.530 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-038-0385.

name: Zinc Carbonate (Smithsonite, ZnCO3)
description: Calcite-structure trigonal zinc carbonate (ZnCO3, smithsonite), major supergene non-sulfide zinc ore mineral and protective passive carbonate layer on weathered galvanized steel and biodegradable Zn implants. Trigonal R-3c (No. 167), a = 4.6526 Å, c = 15.0257 Å, Z = 6, PDF 00-008-0449.

name: Hydrozincite (Zn5(CO3)2(OH)6, Zinc Patina Corrosion Product)
description: Basic zinc carbonate (Zn5(CO3)2(OH)6, hydrozincite), the self-healing white protective patina formed on weathered galvanized steel and architectural zinc roofing in CO2-containing air, characterized by its intense low-angle (200) reflection at 13.06° (d = 6.77 Å). Monoclinic C2/m (No. 12), a = 13.620 Å, b = 6.300 Å, c = 5.420 Å, β = 95.83°, Z = 2, PDF 00-019-1458.

name: Simonkolleite (Zn5(OH)8Cl2·H2O, Marine Zinc Corrosion Product)
description: Layered zinc hydroxychloride hydrate (Zn5(OH)8Cl2·H2O, simonkolleite), the hallmark corrosion product of zinc and galvanized steel in marine/chloride salt-spray environments and zinc-chloride dry-cell cathodes, distinguished by its strong basal (003) peak at 11.22° (d = 7.88 Å). Trigonal R-3m (No. 166), a = 6.3412 Å, c = 23.646 Å, Z = 3, PDF 00-007-0155.

name: Zinc Chloride (δ-ZnCl2, Anhydrous Orthorhombic)
description: Hygroscopic anhydrous zinc dichloride (δ-ZnCl2) built from corner-sharing ZnCl4 tetrahedra in an HCP Cl⁻ sublattice. Used as a hot-dip galvanizing pre-flux, soldering flux, Lewis-acid organic synthesis catalyst, and water-in-salt zinc-ion battery electrolyte. Orthorhombic Pna21 (No. 33), a = 6.443 Å, b = 7.693 Å, c = 6.125 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-042-0589.

name: Zinc Sulfate Anhydrous (Zinkosite, ZnSO4)
description: Anhydrous orthorhombic zinc sulfate (ZnSO4, mineral zinkosite) obtained by roasting sphalerite or dehydrating goslarite above 240 °C. Key intermediate in hydrometallurgical electrowinning of pure Zn and aqueous ZnSO4 zinc-ion battery electrolytes. Orthorhombic Pnma (No. 62), a = 8.588 Å, b = 6.740 Å, c = 4.770 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-008-0491.

name: Zinc Sulfate Heptahydrate (Goslarite, ZnSO4·7H2O)
description: Orthorhombic zinc sulfate heptahydrate (ZnSO4·7H2O, white vitriol / mineral goslarite), isostructural with epsomite (MgSO4·7H2O). Widely used as standard aqueous Zn-ion battery electrolyte salt, micronutrient fertilizer, and zinc electroplating bath reagent. Orthorhombic P212121 (No. 19), a = 11.779 Å, b = 12.050 Å, c = 6.822 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-009-0395.

name: Zinc Ferrite (Franklinite, ZnFe2O4 Normal Spinel)
description: Stoichiometric normal cubic spinel zinc ferrite (ZnFe2O4, mineral franklinite) with Zn²⁺ on tetrahedral A-sites and Fe³⁺ on octahedral B-sites. Paramagnetic at room temperature (antiferromagnetic below TN ≈ 10 K), major phase in electric-arc-furnace (EAF) steelmaking dust and visible-light photocatalysis. Cubic Fd-3m (No. 227), a = 8.4411 Å, Z = 8, PDF 00-022-1012.

name: Zinc Aluminate Spinel (Gahnite, ZnAl2O4)
description: Wide-bandgap (3.8 eV) normal cubic spinel zinc aluminate (ZnAl2O4, mineral gahnite). Distinguished from MgAl2O4 (nearly identical a = 8.085 Å) by the much stronger (220) peak (84% vs 40%) and much weaker (111)/(400) peaks due to heavy tetrahedral Zn²⁺ scattering. Cubic Fd-3m (No. 227), a = 8.0848 Å, Z = 8, PDF 00-005-0669.

name: Zinc Orthosilicate (Willemite, α-Zn2SiO4)
description: Phenakite-structure trigonal zinc orthosilicate (α-Zn2SiO4, mineral willemite). Mn²⁺-doped willemite (P1 phosphor) is the classic high-efficiency green cathodoluminescent and plasma-display phosphor, also prized as a low-loss microwave dielectric ceramic. Trigonal R-3 (No. 148), a = 13.938 Å, c = 9.310 Å, Z = 18, PDF 00-037-1485.

name: Zinc Phosphate Tetrahydrate (Hopeite, α-Zn3(PO4)2·4H2O)
description: Orthorhombic zinc phosphate tetrahydrate (α-Zn3(PO4)2·4H2O, mineral hopeite), the primary crystalline conversion-coating phase on zinc-phosphated automotive steel and galvanized bodies for paint adhesion and corrosion protection, as well as classic dental luting cements. Orthorhombic Pnma (No. 62), a = 10.629 Å, b = 18.339 Å, c = 5.040 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-037-0465.

name: Zinc Nitride (Zn3N2, Anti-Bixbyite Semiconductor)
description: Earth-abundant cubic anti-bixbyite zinc nitride (Zn3N2) with high electron mobility (>100 cm²/V·s) and tunable direct optical bandgap (~1.2–1.5 eV), investigated for thin-film transistors, p-type ZnO doping, and Li-ion conversion anodes. Cubic Ia-3 (No. 206), a = 9.7691 Å, Z = 16, PDF 00-035-0762.

name: Magnesium Alloy AZ91D (Mg-9Al-1Zn Die-Casting Alloy)
description: World's most widely produced cast magnesium alloy (AZ91D: Mg-9wt%Al-0.7wt%Zn-0.2wt%Mn). Consists of Al-supersaturated HCP α-Mg matrix (a = 3.184 Å, c = 5.174 Å, P63/mmc) plus prominent interdendritic cubic β-Mg17Al12 precipitates (36.11° (411/330), 40.08° (332), 43.74° (431)).

name: Magnesium Alloy AM60B (Mg-6Al-0.4Mn Automotive Alloy)
description: High-ductility, crash-energy-absorbing automotive die-casting magnesium alloy (AM60B: Mg-6wt%Al-0.4wt%Mn) with reduced β-Mg17Al12 fraction relative to AZ91D for superior elongation and impact toughness. HCP α-Mg matrix (a = 3.190 Å, c = 5.182 Å, P63/mmc) with minor β-Mg17Al12 (36.11°).

name: Magnesium Alloy ZK60 (Mg-5.5Zn-0.5Zr High-Strength Wrought Alloy)
description: High-strength wrought magnesium extrusion and forging alloy (ZK60-T5: Mg-5.5wt%Zn-0.5wt%Zr) where Zr provides potent grain refinement and Zn forms age-hardening β1'-MgZn2/Mg4Zn7 rod precipitates (40.43°, 41.27°). Also extensively studied for biodegradable load-bearing orthopedic implants. Hexagonal P63/mmc (No. 194), a = 3.198 Å, c = 5.195 Å.

name: Magnesium Alloy ZE41 (Mg-4.2Zn-1.2RE-0.7Zr Sand-Cast Alloy)
description: Aerospace-grade sand-casting magnesium alloy (ZE41A-T5: Mg-4.2wt%Zn-1.2wt%RE-0.7wt%Zr) with excellent pressure-tightness, weldability, and elevated-temperature creep resistance up to 150 °C via grain-boundary T-phase (Mg7Zn3RE) networks. Hexagonal P63/mmc (No. 194), a = 3.204 Å, c = 5.202 Å.

name: Magnesium Alloy Elektron 21 (Mg-2.8Nd-1.3Gd-0.4Zn-0.4Zr)
description: Advanced yttrium-free rare-earth aerospace casting alloy Elektron 21 (EV31A: Mg-2.8wt%Nd-1.3wt%Gd-0.4wt%Zn-0.4wt%Zr) delivering high corrosion resistance, castability, and creep strength to 200 °C. Nd/Gd solutes slightly expand the HCP α-Mg lattice (a = 3.215 Å, c = 5.215 Å). Hexagonal P63/mmc (No. 194).

name: Magnesium-Aluminum Intermetallic (β-Mg17Al12, Alpha-Mn Type)
description: Complex 58-atom α-Mn-type cubic intermetallic β-Mg17Al12 (γ-phase in Mg-Al diagram), the defining secondary phase in AZ91, AZ61, and AM60 magnesium alloys. Controls age hardening, creep softening above 120 °C, and micro-galvanic corrosion kinetics. Cubic I-43m (No. 217), a = 10.5438 Å, Z = 2, PDF 00-001-1128.

name: Magnesium-Calcium Laves Phase (Mg2Ca, C14 Biomedical Alloy Phase)
description: Hexagonal C14 Laves phase Mg2Ca, the biocompatible strengthening eutectic intermetallic in bioresorbable Mg-Ca and Mg-Zn-Ca orthopedic bone implants and ignition-resistant flame-retardant magnesium alloys. Hexagonal P63/mmc (No. 194), a = 6.2386 Å, c = 10.1462 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-013-0450.

name: Magnesium-Yttrium Intermetallic (Mg24Y5, Cubic WE-Series Phase)
description: Alpha-Mn-type cubic equilibrium precipitate Mg24Y5 (ε-phase) occurring in high-yttrium Mg-Y and WE-series (WE43, WE54) heat-resistant aerospace alloys and LPSO-strengthened Mg-Zn-Y alloys. Cubic I-43m (No. 217), a = 11.257 Å, Z = 2, PDF 00-031-0817.

name: Magnesium-Copper Laves Phase (Mg2Cu, Orthorhombic Hydrogen Storage)
description: Orthorhombic Mg2Cu intermetallic used to destabilize MgH2 thermodynamics via the reversible disproportionation reaction 2Mg2Cu + 3H2 ⇌ 3MgH2 + MgCu2, lowering H2 desorption temperature by ~50 °C. Orthorhombic Fddd (No. 70), a = 5.284 Å, b = 9.070 Å, c = 18.250 Å, Z = 16, PDF 00-013-0504.

name: Magnesium-Nickel Intermetallic (Mg2Ni, Hydrogen Storage Alloy)
description: Benchmark hexagonal hydrogen-storage intermetallic Mg2Ni that reversibly absorbs hydrogen to form complex ternary hydride Mg2NiH4 (3.6 wt% H2) with markedly faster kinetics and lower equilibrium desorption temperature (~250 °C) than pure MgH2. Also used in Ni-MH battery negative electrodes. Hexagonal P6222 (No. 180), a = 5.212 Å, c = 13.247 Å, Z = 6, PDF 00-035-1225.

name: Magnesium Diboride (MgB2, 39 K Metallic Superconductor)
description: Simple layered AlB2-type binary metallic superconductor (Tc = 39 K, highest among conventional BCS phonon-mediated ambient-pressure superconductors) composed of graphite-like boron sheets intercalated by Mg²⁺ layers. Deployed in cryogen-free 20 K MRI magnets and fault-current limiters. Hexagonal P6/mmm (No. 191), a = 3.0860 Å, c = 3.5240 Å, Z = 1, PDF 00-038-1369.

name: Magnesium Nitride (α-Mg3N2, Anti-Bixbyite Ceramic)
description: Greenish-yellow cubic anti-bixbyite magnesium nitride (α-Mg3N2) widely used as a high-pressure catalyst for cubic boron nitride (c-BN) synthesis, solid-state nitride phosphor precursor, and ammonia-generation reagent. Cubic Ia-3 (No. 206), a = 9.9657 Å, Z = 16, PDF 00-035-0778.

name: Magnesium Sulfate Heptahydrate (Epsomite, MgSO4·7H2O)
description: Orthorhombic magnesium sulfate heptahydrate (MgSO4·7H2O, Epsom salt / mineral epsomite) composed of octahedral [Mg(H2O)6]²⁺ and SO4²⁻ hydrogen-bonded frameworks. Major evaporite mineral on Earth and Mars, thermochemical heat-storage material, and pharmaceutical/agricultural salt. Orthorhombic P212121 (No. 19), a = 11.868 Å, b = 11.996 Å, c = 6.857 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-036-0419.

name: Magnesium Sulfate Monohydrate (Kieserite, MgSO4·H2O)
description: Monoclinic magnesium sulfate monohydrate (MgSO4·H2O, mineral kieserite), key marine potash-evaporite fertilizer mineral, prominent hydrated sulfate detected across equatorial Mars, and dehydration intermediate of epsomite. Monoclinic C2/c (No. 15), a = 6.912 Å, b = 7.624 Å, c = 7.642 Å, β = 117.70°, Z = 4, PDF 00-033-0882.

name: Magnesium Sulfate Anhydrous (α-MgSO4)
description: Anhydrous orthorhombic α-MgSO4 (CrVO4 structure type) formed by complete dehydration of kieserite above 330 °C. Used as a rapid laboratory desiccant, magnesium oxysulfate (MOS) structural cement reagent, and rechargeable thermochemical heat-storage material. Orthorhombic Cmcm (No. 63), a = 5.182 Å, b = 7.893 Å, c = 6.506 Å, Z = 4, PDF 00-035-0776.

name: Magnesium Chloride Hexahydrate (Bischofite, MgCl2·6H2O)
description: Deliquescent monoclinic magnesium chloride hexahydrate (MgCl2·6H2O, mineral bischofite) harvested from salt lakes and seawater brines. Essential precursor for magnesium oxychloride (Sorel) fireproof cements, phase-change thermal storage (Tm = 117 °C), and dust/ice control. Monoclinic C2/m (No. 12), a = 9.8607 Å, b = 7.1071 Å, c = 6.0737 Å, β = 93.76°, Z = 2, PDF 00-025-0515.

name: Hydromagnesite (Mg5(CO3)4(OH)2·4H2O, Flame-Retardant Mineral)
